semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ الساعة}: two views are possible regarding this maṣdar (verbal noun). First: that it is annexed to its agent, and that on two interpretations. The first interpretation: that it is from the intransitive «زلزل» in the sense of «تزَلْزَلَ» ("to quake"), so the implied meaning is: "the quaking of the Hour". The second interpretation: that it is from the transitive «زَلْزَل», with the object omitted, its implied form being: "the Hour's shaking of people" — so Abū al-Baqāʾ estimated it. Better than this is to estimate it as: "the Hour's shaking of the earth", as indicated by His saying {إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الأرض} [al-Zalzala: 1]. Attributing the quaking or the shaking to the Hour is by way of figurative usage (majāz).
The second view: that the maṣdar is annexed to the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), by way of widening the use of the adverb of time (al-ittisāʿ fī al-ẓarf), as in the saying:
3368 - طَبَّاخِ ساعاتِ الكرى زادَ الكَسِلْ ...
(one who cooks, in the hours of slumber, the provisions of the lazy)
Al-Zamakhsharī clarified that by his saying: "The Hour cannot but be either taken as the agent of it, as though it were what shakes things, by way of predicative figurative usage (al-majāz al-ḥukmī), so that «الزلزلة» is a maṣdar annexed to its agent; or taken as the object, by way of widening the use of the adverb of time and treating it like a direct object, as in His saying, exalted is He: {بَلْ مَكْرُ اليل والنهار} [Sabaʾ: 33]."

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ}: there are several views on it. First: that it is accusative by «تَذْهَلُ»; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else. Second: that it is accusative by «عظيم». Third: that it is accusative by an implied «اذكر» ("remember"). Fourth: that it is a badal (substitute) from «الساعة», and it is given fatḥa only because it is indeclinable (mabnī) on account of its annexation to a verb. This only works according to the view of al-Akhfash; its detailed treatment has preceded at the end of al-Māʾida. Fifth: that it is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from «زلزلة», because each of the event and the time can truly be said to include the other. It is not permissible for it to be accusative by «زلزلة», because of what that entails of separating the maṣdar from what it governs by the khabar (predicate).
His saying: {تَرَوْنَهَا}: there are two views on this pronoun. The more apparent of them: that it is the pronoun of «الزلزلة», because it is what is being spoken about, and His saying {تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ} also supports it. Second: that it is the pronoun of «الساعة». On the first, the distraction and the miscarrying are literal, because it is in this world; on the second it is by way of magnifying and inspiring dread, and [meaning] that it is of this character, since what is meant by «الساعة» is the Resurrection; it is like His saying {يَوْماً يَجْعَلُ الولدان شِيباً} [al-Muzzammil: 17].
His saying: {تَذْهَلُ}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ها» in «تَرَوْنَها», for the seeing here is visual. This only applies on a view other than the first. As for the first view — that «تَذْهَلُ» is what puts «يومَ تَرَوْنَها» in the accusative — the clause has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). Or its position may be the accusative as a ḥāl from «الزلزلة», or from the pronoun in «عظيم», even though it is masculine, because it is the زلزلة in meaning; or from «الساعة», even though it is a muḍāf ilayhi (the genitive term of the construct), because it is either an agent or an object as has preceded. If we make it a ḥāl, there must be an omitted pronoun, its implied form being: «تَذْهَلُ فيها» ("in which … is distracted").
The majority read «تَذْهَلُ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the hāʾ, from «ذَهِل عن كذا يَذْهَلُ». Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Yamānī read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the hāʾ, and with «كل» in the accusative as a direct object, from «أَذْهَلَه عن كذا يُذْهِله», made transitive by the hamza. «الذُّهولُ» is being diverted from a thing. It has been said: when it is accompanied by bewilderment. And it has been said: when that is due to the sudden occurrence of something preoccupying, such as worry, illness and the like. Dhuhl ibn Shaybān [the tribal name] is originally from this.
«المُرْضِعَةُ» is one who is engaged in the act [of suckling], and «المُرْضِعُ» is one whose condition is that she suckles, like «حائض» ("menstruating woman"); when engagement [in the act] is intended, «حائِضة» is said.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why is «مُرْضِعَة» said rather than «مُرْضع»? I say: «المُرْضِعَةُ» is the one who is in the state of suckling, putting her breast in the infant's mouth, and «المرضع» is one whose condition is that she suckles, even if she is not actually suckling at the time she is described by it." The meaning: from the intensity of the terror, this woman is distracted from her child — so how about anyone else? Some of the Kufans said: «المُرْضِعَةُ» is said of the mother, and «المُرْضِعُ» of a hired [wet-nurse] other than the mother. This is refuted by the poet's saying:
3369 - كمُرْضِعَةٍ أولادَ أخرى وضَيَّعَتْ ... بني بطنِها هذا الضلالُ عن القصدِ
(Like a woman suckling another woman's children while she neglected the sons of her own womb — this is straying from the right course)
So he applied «المُرْضِعَة» with the tāʾ to someone other than the mother.
The Arabs' saying «مُرْضِعَة» also refutes the Kufans' saying that adjectives specific to the feminine do not take the feminine tāʾ, such as «حائِض» and «طالق» ("divorced"). What is to be said is: if relation (nasab, i.e. "one characterised by") is intended, the matter is as they mentioned; but if indicating engagement in the act is intended, the tāʾ is obligatory, and one says «حائضة», «طالقة» and «طامِثة».
His saying: {عَمَّآ أَرْضَعَتْ}: «ما» may be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. "from her suckling", and on this there is no need to assume an omission. It may also be in the sense of «الذي» ("that which"), in which case a returning pronoun must have been omitted, i.e. «أَرْضَعَتْه» ("which she suckled"). This is strengthened by «تَضَعُ» being transitive to an object, not a maṣdar. «الحَمْلُ» with fatḥa is what is in a womb or on the top of a tree, and with kasra what is on a back.
His saying: {وَتَرَى الناس سكارى}: the majority read with fatḥa on the tāʾ of «ترى», as addressing a single person. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ [«وتُرِي»], with the agent being the pronoun of «الزلزلة» or «الساعة». On this reading there must be an omitted first object for the meaning to be complete by it, i.e. "and the quake — or the Hour — shows the creation the people drunk". This is supported by the reading of Abū Hurayra, Abū Zurʿa and Abū Nahīk: «تُرَى الناسَ سكارى», with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the rāʾ, in the passive, and «الناسَ» in the accusative. They built it from the verb that is transitive to three objects: the first stands in place of the agent, which is the second-person pronoun, and «الناسَ سُكارى» are the [remaining] first and second.
It may also be transitive to only two, in the sense: "and the quake — or the Hour — shows [the people] a folk who are drunk"; so «الناسَ» is the first and «سكارى» the second.
Al-Zaʿfarānī and ʿAbbās, in his choice [of reading], read «وتُرَى» like the reading of Abū Hurayra, except that they put «الناسُ» in the nominative as the object of the passive verb (nāʾib fāʿil). The feminine in the verb is by their interpreting it as "the group".
The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «سكرى» and «وما هم بسكرى», on the pattern of the feminine adjective of that [meaning]. There is disagreement about it: is it a plural form on the pattern faʿlā like «مَرْضى» and «قَتْلى», or a singular adjective that sufficed for describing the group? It is a well-known disagreement, discussed previously at His saying «أسرى». The apparent sense of Sībawayh's words is that it is a broken plural, for he said: "Some people say «سكرى», making it like «مرضى», because they are both things that come upon a person. Then they made «روبى» like «سكرى» — they are those weighed down by sleep from drinking curdled milk." Al-Fārisī said: "It may properly be the plural of «سَكِر», like «زَمِن» and «زمنى». «رجلٌ سَكِر» has been reported in the sense of «سَكْران», so «سكرى» then comes as the feminine of the plural." I say: among the occurrences of «سَكِر» in the sense of «سَكْران» is the saying:
3370 - وقد جَعَلْتُ إذا ما قُمْتُ يُثْقِلُني ... ثَوْبي فأنهضُ نَهْضَ الشاربِ السَّكِرِ
وكنتُ أَمْشي على رِجْلين مُعْتَدِلاً ... فصِرْتُ أَمْشِي على أخرى من الشَّجر
(Now when I stand, my garment weighs me down, and I rise as the drunken drinker rises; I used to walk upright on two legs, and now I walk on a third made of wood)
The first verse is also narrated «الشارِبِ الثَّمِلِ», but the first is more correct, as the second verse indicates it.
The rest read «سُكارى» with ḍamma on the sīn.
We have previously had, in al-Baqara, a disagreement: is this form a broken plural or a collective noun (ism jamʿ)?
Abū Hurayra, Abū Nahīk and ʿĪsā read with fatḥa on the sīn in both [«سَكارى»], and it is a broken plural whose singular is «سَكْران». Abū Ḥātim said: "It is the dialect of Tamīm."
Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, Abū Zurʿa and al-Aʿmash read «سُكْرى» and «بسُكْرى» with ḍamma on the sīn in both. Ibn Jinnī said: "It is a singular noun like «البُشْرَى». Abū ʿAlī gave me this ruling." Abū al-Faḍl said: "fuʿlā with ḍamma on the fāʾ is an adjective of a single female; but since it was made a description of the people, who are a group, the group was treated like a singular feminine." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is strange." I say: there is nothing strange about it, for fuʿlā with ḍamma on the fāʾ frequently comes in adjectives of the feminine, such as «الربى» and «الحبلى». Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed that it be shortened from «سكارى»; but then this reader ought to have vowelled the kāf with fatḥa, keeping it as it was. Some have indeed narrated it that way from al-Ḥasan. It has also been read «ويرى الناسُ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ and «الناسُ» in the nominative.
Abū Zurʿa, in one narration, read «سَكْرى» with fatḥa and «بسُكْرى» with ḍamma. The same from Ibn Jubayr, except that he dropped the alif from the first but not the second.
Affirming drunkenness and negating it is in the sense of figurative and literal, i.e. "you see the people drunk" by way of comparison, "and they are not drunk" in reality. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was «تَرَوْن» said first, and then «ترى» in the singular? I say: because the seeing was first connected to the quake, so all the people were made seers of it; and lastly it is connected to the people's being in a state of drunkenness, so each one of them must be made a seer of all the rest."

semin-durr:3-3.t: «مَنْ» in {مَن يُجَادِلُ} may be an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), or it may be a relative noun. {فِي الله} means: concerning His attributes. {بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ} is an object or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يُجادل». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «وَتْبَعُ».

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ}: the majority read «كُتِبَ» in the passive and «أنَّ» with fatḥa in both places. There are two views on that. First: that the pronoun and what falls within its scope are in the position of the nominative because they stand in place of the agent [i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]. The hāʾ in «عليه» and in «أنه» both refer back to the preceding «مَنْ». The second «مَنْ» may be conditional with the fāʾ [introducing] its apodosis (jawāb), or it may be a relative noun, with the fāʾ redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) because the mubtadaʾ (subject) resembles a condition. The second «أنَّ» is given fatḥa because it, together with what falls within its scope, is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "then his case and state is that he misleads him". Or «فَأَنَّه» may be estimated as a mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar, i.e. "then for him is that he misleads him".
The second: al-Zamakhsharī said: "Whoever reads with fatḥa, it is because the first is the agent of «كُتِب», and the second is conjoined to it." The Shaykh said: "This is not permissible, because if you make «فأنَّه» conjoined to «أنَّه», «أنَّه» is left without a complete khabar, since «مَنْ» in «مَنْ تَوَلاَّه» is a mubtadaʾ. If you take it to be a relative noun, it has no khabar such that it could stand independently as the khabar of «أنه»; and if you make it conditional, it has no apodosis, since «فأنَّه» has been made conjoined to «أنه»."
I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, went to the like of al-Zamakhsharī's view, for he said: "«وأنَّه» is in the position of the nominative as the object whose agent is not named, and the second «أنَّه» is conjoined to the first, emphasising it like it." And this is a clear refutation [of that].
It has also been read «كَتَبَ» in the active, i.e. "Allah wrote", so «أنَّ» and what falls within its scope are in the position of the accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the rest of the verse is as has preceded.
Al-Aʿmash, and al-Juʿfī from Abū ʿAmr, read «إنه» and «فإنه» with kasra on both hamzas. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Abū ʿAmr read «إنَّه» and «فإنه» with kasra in both", which gives the impression that it is well known from him, and it is not so. On the explanation of this reading there are three views, which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned: that it is a quotation of what was written exactly as it is, as though it were said: "this wording was written concerning him", just as you say: "it was written on it: Indeed Allah is the Rich, the Praiseworthy". Second: that it is on the implication of «قيل» ("it was said"). Third: that «كُتِبَ» contains the sense of «قيل». The Shaykh said: "As for estimating «قيل» — meaning that «عليه» would then be in the position of the object whose agent is not named, and the clause «أنه مَنْ تولاَّه» would be the unnamed-agent object of the implied «قيل» — this is not the doctrine of the Basrans, for according to them a clause can be neither an agent nor the object of a verb whose agent is not named." It seems the Shaykh chose what al-Zamakhsharī began with first, yet it contains what he fled from: namely that he attributed the verb to a clause, so the objection applies to both.
The establishment of the like of this has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. Then he said: "As for the second — meaning that «كُتِب» was made to include (taḍmīn) the sense of saying — it is not the doctrine of the Basrans, because according to them «إنَّ» is only given kasra after explicit saying, not after what has its meaning."
The two pronouns in «عليه» and «أنه» refer back to the first «مَنْ», as has preceded, and likewise the pronouns in «تَوَلاَّه» [i.e. its object pronoun] and «فأنه», and the nominative [pronoun] in «يُضِلُّه» and «يَهْديه», because the first «مَنْ» is the one being spoken about. The nominative pronoun in «تَوَلاَّه» and the accusative in «يُضِلُّه» and «يَهْدِيه» refer back to the second «مَنْ». It has also been said: the pronoun in «عليه» is for "every devil", and the pronoun in «فأنَّه» is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "What appears to me is that the first pronoun, in «أنَّه», refers back to every devil, and that in «فأنَّه» refers back to «مَنْ», which is the one who takes [him] as patron."

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {مِّنَ البعث}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «ريب», and it may be attached to an omitted element as a ṣifa (adjective) of «ريب». Al-Ḥasan read «البَعَث» with fatḥa on the ʿayn [second radical]. It is a dialectal form, like «الطَّرَد» and «الجَلَب» for «الطَّرْد» and «الجَلْب» with sukūn. The Shaykh said: "The Kufans regard making the second radical quiescent as a lightening [which they treat as regular] in what has a guttural letter in its middle, like «النَّهْر» and «النَّهَر», «الشَّعْر» and «الشَّعَر»; the Basrans do not treat it as regular, and what has come of that is, in their view, among the cases in which there are two dialectal forms." I say: the apparent sense of this gives the impression that the original is «البَعَث» with fatḥa and that it was merely lightened, and that is not the case. The point of dispute is only when a word with a guttural is heard with fatḥa on its second radical: may it be made quiescent or not? It is not that every word with a guttural that has come with a quiescent second radical is claimed to have fatḥa originally, as the apparent sense of his wording suggests.
His saying: {مُّخَلَّقَةٍ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ}: the majority read «مُخَلَّقةٍ» and «غير» in the genitive, as naʿt (adjective). Ibn Abī ʿAbla read both in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the indefinite noun, which is very rare, even though Sībawayh treated it as regular.
«العَلَقَةُ» is the clotted piece of blood. It is reported of someone who was asked about the hardest of things that he said: "slipping on «العَلَق»", i.e. on the blood of the slain in battle. «المُضْغَةُ» is a piece of flesh the size of what is chewed, like «الغُرفة» ("scoop") and «الأُكْلة» ("morsel") in the sense of what is scooped and what is eaten. «المُخَلَّقَةُ» is the smooth one with no defect in it, from their saying «صخرةٌ خَلْقاءُ», i.e. smooth; and «خَلَقْتُ السِّواك», "I evened and smoothed the tooth-stick". It has also been said: the doubling in «مُخَلَّقَة» indicates the abundance of creation, because the human being has varied limbs and differing constitutions. This was said by al-Shaʿbī, Qatāda and Abū al-ʿĀliya, and it is a fine meaning.
His saying: {وَنُقِرُّ}: the majority read «ونُقِرُّ» in the nominative, because it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf) and not a reason for what precedes it, such that it would be accusative as conjoined to what precedes it. Yaʿqūb, and ʿĀṣim in one narration, read it in the accusative. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "On the basis that it is conjoined in wording, while the meaning differs, because the lām in «لُنبِيِّنَ» is for reason (taʿlīl), and the lām implied before «نُقِرُّ» is for outcome (ṣayrūra)." This is open to question, because his saying "conjoined in wording" is contradicted by his saying "the implied lām", for implying the lām requires the accusative by an implied «أَنْ» after it, not by conjunction to what precedes it.
Also from ʿĀṣim: «ثم نُخْرِجَكم» with the jīm in the accusative. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «ليبيِّنَ ويَقِرُّ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ in both, the agent being Allah the Exalted, as in the reading with nūn. Yaʿqūb, in one narration, read «ونَقُرُّ» with fatḥa on the nūn, ḍamma on the qāf and the rāʾ in the nominative, from «قَرَّ الماءَ يَقُرُّه», i.e. "he poured it". Abū Zayd the grammarian read «ويَقِرَّ» with fatḥa on the lower-dotted yāʾ, kasra on the qāf and the rāʾ in the accusative, i.e. "and that Allah may settle"; and it is from «قرَّ الماء» when one pours it. In al-Kāmil of Ibn Jubāra: "«لِنُبَيِّن ونُقِرَّ ثم نُخْرِجَكم» with the accusative in all of them — meaning, and with nūn in all — al-Mufaḍḍal. With yāʾ in both together with the accusative: Abū Ḥātim; and with yāʾ and the nominative: ʿUmar ibn Shabba." End of quotation. [Translator's note: the quotation from al-Kāmil is elliptical in the source; it is translated as written, the names being those of the transmitters of each variant.]
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The reading in the nominative is a report that He, exalted is He, settles in the wombs whatever He wills to settle." Then he said: "The reading in the accusative is a reason (taʿlīl) conjoined to a reason. Its meaning: We created you in stages, and this gradation is for two purposes (gharaḍ). One of them: that We may make Our power clear. The second: that We may settle in the wombs whom We settle; then they are born, grow up and reach the age of legal responsibility, and I make them responsible. This reading is supported by His saying {ثُمَّ لتبلغوا أَشُدَّكُمْ}."
I say: calling such acts attributed to Allah the Exalted a "purpose" (gharaḍ) is not permissible.
Ibn Waththāb read «نِشاء» with kasra on the nūn, which is the kasra of the imperfect prefix; that has preceded at the first occurrence of this topic.
His saying: {طِفْلاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «نُخْرِجكم». It is singular only because it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), like «الرِّضا» and «العَدْل», so the singular and masculine are required — al-Mubarrad said this; or because the genus is intended by it; or because the meaning is: He brings out each one of you, as in "a loaf satisfies the people", i.e. each one of them. It may also be made to agree with what is intended by it, so one says «طفلان» and «أطفال»; in the ḥadīth: "He was asked about the «أطفال» (children) of the polytheists." «الطِّفْلُ» is applied to the child from the time of separation [from the womb] until puberty. As for «الطَفْل» with fatḥa, it is "the soft/delicate", and a woman is «طَفْلة». He said:
3371 - ولقد لَهَوْتُ بِطَفْلةٍ مَيَّالَةٍ ... بَلْهاءَ تُطْلِعُني على أَسْرارِها
(I have dallied with a soft, swaying, guileless woman who let me in on her secrets)
As for «الطَّفَل» with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ and the fāʾ, it is the time after ʿaṣr, from their saying «طَفَلَت الشمسُ» when the sun inclines towards setting. And «أطفلتِ المرأةُ», i.e. she came to have a child.
A group read «يَتَوَفَّى» with fatḥa on the yāʾ. There are two explanations of it. First: that the agent is the pronoun of the Creator, exalted is He, i.e. "Allah the Exalted takes him in death"; so al-Zamakhsharī estimated it. Second: that the agent is the pronoun of «مَنْ», i.e. "he completes his term". This reading is like the one in al-Baqara: {والذين يَتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكُمْ} [verse 234], i.e. their period.
It is reported from Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ that they read «العُمْر» with the second radical quiescent, which is a regular lightening, like «عُنْق» for «عُنُق».
His saying: {لِكَيْلاَ}: attached to «يُرَدُّ». Its parallel has preceded in al-Naḥl.
«هامدةً» is accusative as a ḥāl, because the seeing is visual. «الهُمُود» is stillness and lowliness. «هَمَدَت الأرضُ»: the earth dried up and became effaced. «هَمَدَ الثوبُ»: the garment wore out. Al-Aʿshā said:
3372 - قالَتْ قُتَيْلَةُ ما لجِسْمِكَ شاحباً ... وأرى ثيابَكَ بالِياتٍ هُمَّدا
(Qutayla said: Why is your body pale, and I see your garments worn out and tattered?)
«الاهتزازُ» is moving, and it is used figuratively here for the earth's bringing forth its vegetation by means of water. The majority read «رَبَتْ», i.e. "it increased", from «رَبا يَرْبُو». Abū Jaʿfar, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, and Abū ʿAmr in one narration read «وَرَبَأَت» with hamza, i.e. "it rose". One says «رَبَأَ بنفسه عن كذا», i.e. he rose above it. From it is «الرَّبِيئَةُ», the one who goes up on a high place to watch for the people what is coming upon them; he is also called «رَبِيْءٌ». The poet said:
3373 - بَعَثْنا رَبِيْئاً قبلَ ذلك مُخْمِلاً ... كذئب الغضى يمشي الضَّراء ويَتَّقي
(Before that we sent out a scout, keeping himself hidden, like the wolf of the ghaḍā thicket, creeping through cover and wary)
His saying: {مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ}: there are two views on it. First: that it is a ṣifa of the omitted object, its implied form being: "and it brought forth colours, or kinds, of every kind". Second: that «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "it brought forth every kind"; this works according to the Kufans and al-Akhfash.
«البهيجُ» is the beautiful which delights the one looking at it. «بَهُجَ» with ḍamma, «بَهاجَةً» and «بَهْجَة», i.e. it was beautiful; and «أبهجني كذا», i.e. it delighted me with its beauty.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {ذلك}: there are three views on it. First: that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is the prepositional phrase after it. What is pointed to is what preceded of the creation of the children of Adam and their development through stages. The implied meaning: "That which We mentioned of the creation of the children of Adam and their development comes about because Allah is the Truth, and because He …" to the end. Second: that «ذلك» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is that". Third: that «ذلك» is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "We did that because Allah is the Truth". So the bāʾ [phrase] on the first view is in the position of the nominative, and on the second and third in the position of the accusative.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {وَأَنَّ الساعة آتِيَةٌ}: there are two views on it. First: that it is conjoined to what is made genitive by the bāʾ, i.e. "that is because the Hour …". Second: that it is neither conjoined to it nor included within the scope of causation; rather it is a khabar (predicate), and the mubtadaʾ (subject) is omitted because the meaning is understood, the implied form being: "and the matter is that the Hour …". As for «لا ريبَ فيها», this clause may be a second khabar, or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial).

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {ومِنَ الناس}: Ibn ʿAṭiyya made this wāw the wāw of ḥāl (circumstance), for he said: "It is as though He is saying: these examples are utterly clear, and yet among people there is one who disputes. So it is as though the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl, while in the preceding verse the wāw is a conjunctive wāw." The Shaykh said: "It is not to be imagined that the wāw in {ومِنَ الناس مَن يُجَادِلُ} is a wāw of ḥāl; and on the assumption of the clause he estimated before it, were it explicit, it cannot be paraphrased with «إذ», so it is not for ḥāl but for conjunction." I say: his preventing its paraphrase with «إذ» is open to question, since if it were so paraphrased, nothing objectionable would follow from it.
His saying: {بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ}: it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يُجادِلُ», or attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the agent of «يجادل», i.e. "he disputes while being without knowledge", i.e. ignorant.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {ثَانِيَ عِطْفِهِ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يُجادل», i.e. "turning aside". It is a verbal [non-defining] annexation (iḍāfa lafẓiyya), like {مُّمْطِرُنَا}. The majority read it with kasra on the ʿayn [«عِطْف»], which is the side; it is a metonymy for arrogance. Al-Ḥasan read it with fatḥa on the ʿayn [«عَطْف»], a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of showing kindness, and it describes him [by its negation, i.e.] with hardness.
His saying: {لِيُضِلَّ}: attached either to «يُجادِلُ» or to «ثانيَ عِطْفِهِ». The majority read «يُضِلُّ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, the object being omitted, i.e. "to lead others astray". Mujāhid, and Abū ʿAmr in one narration, read it with fatḥa, i.e. "that he himself may go astray".
His saying: {لَهُ فِي الدنيا خِزْيٌ}: this clause may be a simultaneous ḥāl, i.e. "deserving that", or an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), or it may be resumptive (mustaʾnafa). Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «وأُذِيْقُه» with the hamza of the first person. «وعذابَ الحريق» may be an instance of annexing the qualified noun to its adjective, since the original is «العذاب الحريق», i.e. «المُحْرِق» ("the burning"), like «السَّميع» in the sense of «المُسْمِع».

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {ذلك بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ}: like His saying {ذلك بِأَنَّ الله} [verse 6]. Likewise His saying {وَأَنَّ الله}: it may be conjoined to the cause; or the implied form may be: "and the matter is that Allah …", so that it is cut off from what precedes it.
His saying «ظَلاَّمٍ» is an intensive form (mithāl mubālagha). If you say «ليس زيدٌ بظلاَّمٍ» ("Zayd is not a great wrongdoer"), it does not follow from it that the basic wrongdoing is negated, for negating the more specific does not entail negating the more general. The answer: the intensive form was brought only because of the multiplicity of its objects, for «العبيد» is a plural. Better than this is that faʿʿāl here is for relation (nasab), i.e. "[not] possessing wrongdoing", not for intensity.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {على حَرْفٍ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَعْبُدُ», i.e. "wavering". The meaning of «على حرف» is: in doubt, or in deviation, or on the edge of the religion and not in its middle, like one who is at the edge of an army: if he sees good he stands firm, otherwise he flees.
His saying: {خَسِرَ}: the majority read «خَسِرَ» as a past verb. It admits three views: resumption (istiʾnāf); being a ḥāl from the agent of «انقلبَ» — and there is no need to imply «قد» according to the correct view; and being a badal (substitute) from His saying «انقلَبَ», just as the imperfect is substituted for its like in His saying {يَلْقَ أَثَاماً يُضَاعَفْ} [al-Furqān: 69].
Mujāhid, al-Aʿraj, Ibn Muḥayṣin and al-Jaḥdarī, among others, read «خاسِرَ» in the form of an active participle, accusative as a ḥāl, and this supports the past verb in the majority reading being a ḥāl. It has also been read in the nominative [«خاسِرُ»], and there are two views on it. First: that it is the agent of «انقلبَ», by putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, i.e. "the loser of this world turned back", the original being «انقلبَ هو». Second: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "he is the loser of …". This reading supports resumption in the past-tense reading, on the second explanation. Whoever reads «خاسر» in the nominative or the accusative ought to put «الآخرةِ» in the genitive, as conjoined to «الدنيا», which is genitive by annexation. The accusative may also remain in it, since «الدنيا» may be accusative, the tanwīn having been dropped from «خاسر» only because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as in the saying:
3374 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا ذاكرَ اللهَ إلاَّ قليلا
(… nor one who remembers Allah except a little)

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {يَدْعُو لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أَقْرَبُ مِن نَّفْعِهِ}: there are ten views on it. That is because either «يَدْعُو» is made to govern the clause {لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أَقْرَبُ مِن نَّفْعِهِ}, or not. If we make it govern it, there are seven views.
First: that «يَدْعُو» is in the sense of «يَقُول» ("he says"), the lām is the lām of ibtidāʾ (inception), and «مَنْ» is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); «ضَرُّه» is a second mubtadaʾ and «أقربُ» its khabar (predicate). This clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the khabar of the relative noun is omitted, its implied form being: "he says: the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit is a god", or "my god", or the like. The whole clause is in the position of the accusative by «يَدْعُو», because it is in the sense of «يَقُول», so it is quoted by it. This is the view of Abū al-Ḥasan [al-Akhfash]. On this view His saying {لَبِئْسَ المولى} is resumptive and not included in what is quoted before it, because the disbelievers do not say that about their idols. Some have rejected this view as being corrupt in meaning, since the disbeliever does not believe at all of the idols that their harm is nearer than their benefit.
Second: that «يَدْعُو» is likened to the verbs of the heart (afʿāl al-qulūb), because invoking only proceeds from a belief; and the verbs of the heart can be suspended (tuʿallaq), so «يَدْعُو» is likewise suspended by the lām. «مَنْ» is a relative noun as mubtadaʾ, the clause after it is its ṣila, and its khabar is omitted as in the previous view. The clause is in the position of the accusative, as it is after verbs of the heart.
Third: that «يَدْعُو» is made to include (taḍmīn) the sense of «يزعم» ("he claims"), so it is suspended as that is suspended; the discussion of it is like that of the previous view.
Fourth: that all verbs may be suspended, whether verbs of the heart or others, so the lām suspends «يَدْعو»; this is the doctrine of Yūnus. The discussion of the clause after it is as has preceded.
Fifth: that «يَدْعو» is in the sense of «يُسَمِّي» ("he names"), so the lām is added to the first object, which is the relative noun with its ṣila, and the second object is omitted, its implied form being: "he names the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit a god and an object of worship", and the like.
Sixth: that the lām has been displaced from its position. The original is «يَدْعُو مَنْ لَضَرُّه أقربُ», and it was brought forward from a later position. This is the view of al-Farrāʾ. They rejected this on the ground that what is within the ṣila of a relative noun does not precede the relative noun.
Seventh: that the lām is redundant (zāʾida) in the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), which is «مَنْ». The implied form: «يَدْعُو مَنْ ضَرُّه أقرب». So «مَنْ» is a relative noun, the clause after it is its ṣila, and the relative noun is the object of «يَدْعُو», to which the lām was added, as it is added in His saying {رَدِفَ لَكُم} [al-Naml: 72] on one of the two views. This has been rejected on the ground that the lām is added only when the governor is secondary (farʿ) [e.g. a participle or maṣdar], or when the governed word is brought forward. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «يَدْعُو مَنْ ضَرُّه» without the lām of ibtidāʾ, which supports this view.
If you do not make it govern the clause after it, there are three views on it. The most apparent of them: that the second «يَدْعُو» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first «يَدْعو», so it governs nothing, as though it were said: "he invokes, he invokes, besides Allah, that which neither harms him nor benefits him".
On this view, the clause {ذلك هُوَ الضلال} is parenthetical (muʿtariḍa) between the emphasised and the emphasis, because it contains reinforcement and emphasis of the speech, and His saying {لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ} is a resumptive statement. So the lām is for ibtidāʾ, «مَنْ» is a relative noun, «ضَرُّه» is a mubtadaʾ and «أقربُ» its khabar, the clause being the ṣila, and «لَبِئْسَ» is the reply of an implied oath; this implied oath and its reply are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, which is the relative noun.
Second: that «ذلك» is made a relative noun in the sense of «الذي», «هو» a mubtadaʾ and «الضلالُ» its khabar, the clause being the ṣila. This relative noun with its ṣila is in the position of the accusative as the object of «يَدْعو», i.e. "he invokes that which is the error". This is transmitted from Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī. This does not work on the opinion of the Basrans, since according to them no demonstrative is a relative noun except «ذا», under conditions I mentioned previously. As for the Kufans, they allow demonstratives in general to be relative nouns. On this view «لَمَنْ ضَرُّه أَقْرَبُ» is resumptive, as has been established.
Third: that «ذلك» is made a mubtadaʾ. As for «هو», they allowed it to be a badal (substitute), a separating pronoun (faṣl), or a mubtadaʾ; «الضلالُ» is the khabar of «ذلك» or the khabar of «هو», according to the disagreement about «هو»; and «يَدْعُو» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), with its returning pronoun omitted, its implied form being «يَدْعوه». They paraphrased this verb standing in the place of a ḥāl as «مَدْعُوَّاً» ("invoked"). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak", and did not explain the reason for its weakness. It seems the reason is that «يَدْعُو» is active, so it is not fitting to paraphrase the ḥāl standing in its place as a passive participle; rather what is fitting is to paraphrase it as an active participle, so they should have paraphrased it as «داعياً». Had the construction been «يُدعى» in the passive, their paraphrase «مَدْعُوَّاً» would have been good. Do you not see that if you say «جاء زيدٌ يضربُ» ("Zayd came, striking"), you paraphrase it with «ضارب», not with «مَضْروب»?
The one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-al-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being: "evil indeed is the patron, and evil indeed is the companion — that invoked one".

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {مَن كَانَ}: it may be conditional, which is the apparent sense, or it may be a relative noun. His saying {فَلْيَمْدُدْ} is either the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition or the khabar (predicate) of the relative noun, the fāʾ being because of its likeness to a condition.
The majority read the lām of «لِيَقْطَعْ» with kasra; some made it quiescent, as they make it quiescent after fāʾ and wāw, since they are all conjunctions. Likewise they treated «ثم» like those two in making the hāʾ of «هو» and «هي» quiescent after it; this is the reading of al-Kisāʾī, and of Nāfiʿ in the narration of Qālūn from him.
His saying: {هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ}: the interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), because «النظر» is suspended by interrogation, and when it is in the sense of reflection it is made transitive with «في». His saying {مَا يَغِيظُ}: «ما» is a relative noun in the sense of «الذي», and the returning pronoun is the latent (mustatir) pronoun. «ما» with its ṣila is the object of His saying «يُذْهِبَنَّ», i.e. "will his scheme remove the thing that enrages him?" So the nominative [pronoun] in «يَغيظه» refers back to «الذي», and the accusative to «مَنْ كان يظن».
The Shaykh said: "«ما» in «ما يَغيظ» is in the sense of «الذي», with the returning pronoun omitted; or it is maṣdariyya." I say: neither of these two statements is correct. As for his saying "the returning pronoun is omitted", it is not so; rather it is an implied latent pronoun having the status of something present, as was established before that; "omitted" is said only of what is in the position of the accusative or genitive. As for his saying "or maṣdariyya", that is not so either, since if it were maṣdariyya it would be a particle according to the correct view, and if it is a particle no pronoun refers back to it, and if no pronoun refers back to it, the verb is left without an agent. If you say: I imply in «يَغيظ» an agent pronoun referring back to «مَنْ كان يظنُّ» — the answer is that «مَنْ كان يظنُّ» is, in meaning, the one enraged, not the one enraging. This is a fine investigation, so reflect on it.
As for the pronoun in «يَنْصُرَه», the apparent view is that it refers back to «مَنْ», and «النصر» has been explained as provision. It has also been said: it refers back to the religion and Islam, so «النصر» is in its proper sense [help/victory].

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {وكذلك أَنزَلْنَاهُ}: the kāf is either a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of the implied maṣdar, or a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, according to the disagreement that has preceded, i.e. "and like that sending down We sent down the whole Qurʾān as clear signs". So «آياتٍ» is a ḥāl.
His saying: {وَأَنَّ الله يَهْدِي}: three views are possible regarding «أنَّ». First: that it is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the object of «أَنْزَلْناه», i.e. "and We sent down that Allah guides whom He wills", i.e. We sent down Allah's guidance for the one whose guidance He wills. Second: that it is on the omission of a preposition, that preposition being attached to an omitted element. The implied form: "and because Allah guides whom He wills, We sent it down"; so the two well-known views about its position apply: is it in the position of the accusative or the genitive? Al-Zamakhsharī went to this, and said in estimating it: "And because Allah guides by it those whom He knows will believe, He sent it down thus, made clear." Third: that it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "and the matter is that Allah guides whom He wills".

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {إِنَّ الذين آمَنُواْ}: there are three views on the verse. First: that the second «إنَّ» with its noun and khabar (predicate) is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the first «إنَّ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«إنَّ» was brought in on each of the two parts of the sentence for additional emphasis. Similar to it is the saying of Jarīr:
3375 - إنَّ الخليفةَ إنَّ اللهَ سَرْبلَه ... سِرْبالَ مُلْكٍ به تُرْجَى الخواتيمُ
(Indeed the Caliph — indeed Allah has clothed him in a garment of kingship by which good endings are hoped for)"
The Shaykh said: "The apparent sense of this is that he likened the verse to the line, and al-Zajjāj likewise coupled it with the verse. But the line is not necessarily like the verse, because in the line it is possible that the khabar of «الخليفةَ» is «به ترجى الخواتيمُ», and that «إنَّ اللهَ سَرْبَله» is a parenthetical clause between the noun of «إنَّ» and its khabar — unlike the verse, for there His saying {إِنَّ الله يَفْصِلُ} is the only possibility. What made it good for «إنَّ» to come on the clause serving as khabar is the length of the separation between them by the conjoined items."
I say: his saying "for there His saying «إن الله يَفْصِل» is the only possibility", meaning as khabar, is not so, because the verse admits two other views which people have mentioned. The first: that the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "they will be separated on the Day of Resurrection" or the like, and what is mentioned is an explanation of it; so Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. The second: that the second «إنَّ» is a repetition of the first by way of emphasis. This conforms to the rule that when a particle is repeated for emphasis, what was attached to it, or the pronoun of what was attached to it, is repeated with it; and here what was attached to it first has been repeated with it, namely the Majestic Name [Translator's note: as written in the source; in the verse the first «إنَّ» is followed by «الذين آمنوا», and the Majestic Name follows the second]. So it is not the only possibility that His saying {إِنَّ الله يَفْصِلُ} is the khabar of the first «إنَّ», as was stated.
The explanation of the words of this verse has preceded, except «المجوس» (the Magians). They are a people about whom the scholars have disagreed. It has been said: a people who worship fire. It has been said: the sun and the moon. It has been said: they separated from the Christians and wore haircloth. It has been said: they took something from the religion of the Christians and something from the religion of the Jews, and they are those who hold that the world has two principles: light and darkness. And it has been said: they are a people who make use of impurities, and the original is «نَجوس» with nūn, which was changed into mīm.

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {وَكَثِيرٌ مِّنَ الناس}: there are several views on it. First: that it is nominative by an implied verb, its implied form being: "and many of the people prostrate to Him". This is according to those who forbid using a homonym in both its meanings, or combining the literal and the figurative in a single word. That is because the prostration attributed to non-rational beings is other than the prostration attributed to rational beings, so «كثيرٌ من الناس» is not conjoined to what precedes it, because the verb attributed to them differs in meaning. Do you not see that the prostration of non-rational beings is obedience and submission to His command, while the prostration of rational beings is this specific form?
Second: that it is conjoined to what precedes it. On that there are three interpretations. First: that what is meant by prostration is the common element shared by all, rational and otherwise, namely submission and obedience; this belongs to semantic commonality (ishtirāk maʿnawī). The second interpretation: that it is a homonym in the verbal sense (ishtirāk lafẓī), and it is permissible to use a homonym in both its meanings. The third interpretation: that the prostration attributed to rational beings is literal and to others figurative, and it is permissible to combine the literal and the figurative. There is disagreement on these matters; establishing them belongs to a place more suited to it than this.
The third of the aforementioned views: that «كثيرٌ» is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, namely «مُثابٌ» ("rewarded"), as indicated by the khabar of its counterpart, His saying {وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ العذاب}; so al-Zamakhsharī estimated it. Abū al-Baqāʾ estimated it as: "obedient, or rewarded, or the like".
Fourth: that «كثيرٌ» is likewise nominative as mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is «من الناس», i.e. "of the people who are truly people", namely the righteous and the God-fearing.
Fifth: that it is likewise nominative as mubtadaʾ, with exaggeration in multiplying those deserving punishment: «كثيرٌ» is conjoined to «كثير», and then {حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ العذاب} is given as a khabar about them. Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned that. The Shaykh, after relating these last two explanations from al-Zamakhsharī, said: "These two explanations are weak", and did not explain why they are weak.
I say: as for the first of them, there is no doubt of its weakness, since there is no substantial benefit in reporting that. As for the second, [its sense] may become apparent: repetition conveys multiplicity, and it is close to their saying "I have a thousand and a thousand", and the saying:
3376 - لو عُدَّ قبرٌ وقبرٌ كنتَ أَكْرَمَهم ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Were grave after grave counted, you would be the noblest of them …)
Al-Zuhrī read «والدَّوابُ» with the bāʾ unstressed. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its justification is that he dropped the first bāʾ out of dislike for the doubling and for combining two quiescent letters." Janāḥ ibn Ḥubaysh read «وكبيرٌ» with the one-dotted bāʾ. It has also been read «وكثيرٌ حَقَّاً» in the accusative.
What puts it in the accusative is omitted, and it is the khabar, its implied form being: "and many — punishment has become due upon them truly", with «العذابُ» nominative as agent. It has also been read «حُقَّ» in the passive.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "{وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ العذاب} may be conjoined to what precedes, i.e. and many upon whom punishment has become due prostrate — i.e. reluctantly and against their will: either by their shadow, or by their submission in times of hardship." I say: his saying "conjoined to what precedes" means conjunction of sentences, not that it alone is conjoined to what precedes, as evidenced by his estimating it as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «يَسْجد».
His saying: {وَمَن يُهِنِ الله}: «مَنْ» is a fronted object, and it is conditional; its apodosis is the fāʾ with what follows it. The majority read «مُكْرِمٍ» with kasra on the rāʾ as an active participle. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with fatḥa, which is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), i.e. "then he has no honouring".

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {هذان خَصْمَانِ}: «الخَصْم» is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); for that reason it is mostly kept singular and masculine, and on that is His saying, exalted is He: {نَبَأُ الخصم إِذْ تَسَوَّرُواْ} [Ṣād: 21]. It may also be put in the dual, the plural and the feminine, and on that is this verse. Since each «خَصْم» is a party comprising a group, He said «اختصَمُوا» in the plural form, like His saying {وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ المؤمنين اقتتلوا} [al-Ḥujurāt: 9]; so the plural is out of regard for the meaning.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «اختصما» out of regard for its wording, and it contradicts the written text (al-sawād). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Most usage keeps it singular; whoever puts it in the dual and plural treats it like adjectives and nouns; and «اختصموا» is put in the plural only by treatment according to meaning, because each disputant is [a party] comprising individuals." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«الخصم» is an adjective with which the band or the party is described, so it is as though it were said: these are two bands, or two parties, disputing. His saying «هذان» is according to the wording, and «اختصموا» according to the meaning, like His saying {وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ حتى إِذَا خَرَجُواْ} [Muḥammad: 16]. Had it been said «هؤلاء خصمان» or «اختصما», it would be permissible for the believers and the disbelievers to be meant." I say: if by his saying "«خَصْم» is an adjective" he meant by way of figurative usage, that is granted, because maṣdars are frequently used as descriptions; but if he meant that it is an adjective in reality, his error is evident, since they state explicitly that the like of «رجلٌ خصمٌ» is like «رجلٌ عَدْل». His saying "«هذان» is according to the wording" means: they were pointed to with the dual demonstrative, even though in reality the plural is meant, by consideration of the wording "the two bands", "the two parties" and the like. His saying "like His saying {وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَسْتَمِعُ} …" to the end is open to question, because in that verse something that has a wording and a meaning precedes, namely «مَنْ», whereas here nothing that has a wording and a meaning precedes. His saying, exalted is He, {فِي رَبِّهِمْ} means "concerning the religion of their Lord", so a muḍāf must have been omitted.
Al-Kisāʾī, in one narration from him, read «خِصمان» with kasra on the khāʾ. His saying {فالذين كَفَرُواْ}: this clause is a detailing and clarification of the settling of the dispute meant by His saying, exalted is He, {إِنَّ الله يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ} [verse 17] — al-Zamakhsharī said this. On this view {هذان خَصْمَانِ} is parenthetical. The clause «اختصموا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and not an emphasising one, because it is more specific than the absolute dispute understood from «خصمان».
Al-Zaʿfarānī, in his choice [of reading], read «قُطِعَتْ» with the ṭāʾ unstressed. The well-known reading conveys multiplicity, and this one admits it.
His saying: {يُصَبُّ}: this clause may be a second khabar (predicate) of the relative noun, a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لهم», or resumptive (mustaʾnafa).

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {يُصْهَرُ}: a clause that is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الحميم». «الصَّهْرُ» is melting. One says «صَهَرْتُ الشحم», i.e. I melted the fat; «الصُّهارة» is the melted fat-tail; and «صَهَرَتْهُ الشمسُ», the sun melted it with its heat. He said:
3377 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تَصْهَرُه الشمسُ فما يَنْصَهِرْ
(… the sun scorches it, yet it does not melt)
The in-law (al-ṣihr) is called «صِهْر» because of his blending with his in-laws, as an image of the intensity of mixing. Al-Ḥasan, among others, read «يُصَهَّرُ» with fatḥa on the ṣād and doubling of the hāʾ, for intensity and multiplicity of that.
His saying: {والجلود}: there are two views on it. The more apparent of them: that it is conjoined to the relative «ما», i.e. "what is in their bellies of the intestines is melted, and the skins are melted too", i.e. their outside and their inside are melted. Second: that it is nominative by an implied verb, i.e. "and the skins are burnt". They said: because skin does not melt; it only contracts and shrivels when exposed to fire. In the implication it is like the saying:
3378 - عَلَفْتُها تِبْناً وماءً بارداً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I fed her straw and cold water …)
[and the saying]
3379 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وزَجَّجْنَ الحواجبَ والعيونا
(… and they plucked fine their eyebrows, and the eyes)
[and His saying, exalted is He]: {والذين تَبَوَّءُوا الدار والإيمان} [al-Ḥashr: 9]. For these are on the implied form: "and I gave her water to drink", "and they applied kohl to the eyes", and "and they embraced faith".

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {وَلَهُمْ مَّقَامِعُ}: two views are possible regarding this pronoun. The more apparent of them: that it refers back to those who disbelieved; on that, there are two views about the lām. First: that it is for entitlement (istiḥqāq). Second: that it is in the sense of «على» ("against"), like His saying {لَهُمُ اللعنة} [al-Raʿd: 25]; and this is of no account. The second view: that the pronoun refers back to the Zabāniya, the keepers of Hell, the context of the speech indicating them; and this is far-fetched. «مِنْ حديدٍ» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «مقامِع», which is the plural of «مِقْمَعَة» with kasra on the mīm, because it is the instrument of «القمع» (subduing). One says «قَمَعَه يَقْمَعُه» when one strikes him with something to restrain and humiliate him. «المِقْمَعَةُ» is the hammer; and it has been said: the whip.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {كُلَّمَآ أرادوا}: «كلَّ» is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf). The discussion establishing it has preceded in al-Baqara. What governs it here is His saying {أُعِيدُواْ}. As for {مِنْ غَمٍّ}, there are two views on it. First: that it is a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in «منها», with the governor repeated, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), like His saying {لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بالرحمن لِبُيُوتِهِمْ} [al-Zukhruf: 33]. But a badal of inclusion must have a linking pronoun, and there is none, so they said: it is implied, its implied form being «مِنْ غَمِّها» ("from its anguish"). Second: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); since one of the conditions for the accusative is lacking, it was made genitive by the preposition of cause. That condition is the identity of the agent [which is absent here]: the agent of going out is other than the agent of the anguish, for the anguish is from the Fire and the going out is from the disbelievers.
His saying: {وَذُوقُواْ}: it is in the accusative [i.e. object position] by an implied verb of saying conjoined to «أُعِيْدُوا», i.e. "and it is said to them: taste!"

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {يُحَلَّوْنَ}: the majority read with yāʾ and fatḥa on the lām, doubled, from «حَلاَّه يُحَلِّيه» when he clothed him in ornaments. It has also been read with sukūn on the ḥāʾ and fatḥa on the unstressed lām [«يُحْلَوْن»], which has the sense of the first, as though they made it transitive sometimes by doubling and sometimes by the hamza. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "From your saying «أحلى», i.e. he clothed in ornaments, and it has the sense of the doubled form."
Ibn ʿAbbās read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, sukūn on the ḥāʾ and fatḥa on the unstressed lām [«يَحْلَوْن»]. There are three views on it. First: that it is from «حَلِيَتْ المرأةُ تَحْلَى» so she is «حالٍ», and likewise «حَلِيَ الرجلُ» so he is «حالٍ», when they wore ornaments or came to have ornaments [Translator's note: the source has «صارا دونَ حُلِيّ», literally "became without ornaments", which is likely a corruption of «ذَوَيْ حُلِيّ»; the sense of "came to have ornaments" is given]. Second: that it is from «حَلِيَ بعيني كذا يَحْلَى» when you find it beautiful, with «مِنْ» redundant in His saying {مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ}. He said: "So the meaning is: they find beautiful in it the bracelets that are worn." When the Shaykh transmitted this view from Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī, he said: "This is not good, because he made «حَلِيَ» a transitive verb, and for that reason he judged «مِنْ» to be redundant in an affirmative context, which is not the doctrine of the Basrans. On this assumption it ought not to be permissible, because it is not attested in this sense except as intransitive. If it is in this sense, «مِنْ» is causal, i.e. by wearing bracelets of gold they become beautiful in the eyes of whoever sees them, i.e. some of them become beautiful in the eyes of others."
I say: what he transmitted from Abū al-Faḍl was also said by Abū al-Baqāʾ, who allowed another view regarding the verb's object, for he said: "It may be from «حَلِيَ بعيني كذا» when it is beautiful, with «مِنْ» redundant; or the object may be omitted, and «مِنْ أساورَ» is a naʿt (adjective) of it." So he judged it to be transitive and nothing else, and allowed the two mentioned views concerning the object.
Third: that it is from «حَلِيَ بكذا» when one obtains it, so the implied form is «يَحْلَوْن بأساورَ», with «مِنْ» in the sense of the bāʾ. Among the occurrences of «حَلِيَ» in the sense of «ظَفِرَ» ("to obtain") is their saying «لم يَحْلَ فلانٌ بطائلٍ», i.e. he obtained nothing worthwhile. Know that «حَلِيَ» in the sense of wearing ornament, or in the sense of obtaining, is from a root with yāʾ, because both are from «الحِلْيَة» (ornament). As for «حَلِيَ بعيني كذا», it is from a root with wāw, because it is from «الحلاوة» (sweetness); the wāw was changed into a yāʾ only because of the kasra before it.
His saying: {مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ}: on the first «مِنْ» there are three views. First: that it is redundant (zāʾida), as has been established from al-Rāzī and Abū al-Baqāʾ, even though it is not among the principles of the Basrans. Second: that it is partitive (tabʿīḍ), i.e. some bracelets. Third: that it is for clarifying the genus (bayān al-jins); Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this, and began with it. This is open to question, since nothing vague precedes. As for «مِنْ ذهب», [the «مِنْ»] is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), and it is a naʿt of «أساور», as has preceded.
Ibn ʿAbbās read «مِنْ أَسَوِرَ» without alif and without hāʾ; it is shortened from «أساوِر», as [in] «جَنَدِلٍ», the original being «جَنادِل». The Shaykh said: "Its analogy would have been to make it triptote, because its pattern has been reduced so that it became like «جَنَدِلٍ»; but he regarded the omitted element as present, so he made it diptote."
I say: so he made the tanwīn in «جَنَدِلٍ», shortened from «جنادل», a tanwīn of triptosis (tanwīn al-ṣarf). Some grammarians have stated explicitly that it is a tanwīn of compensation (tanwīn ʿiwaḍ), as it is in «جَوارٍ» and «غَواشٍ» and their category.
His saying: {وَلُؤْلُؤاً}: Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read it in the accusative; the rest in the genitive. As for the accusative, there are four views on it. First: that it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being: "and they are given pearls". Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned nothing else, and likewise Abū al-Fatḥ interpreted it by an implied verb. Second: that it is accusative as conjoined to the position of «مِنْ أساور»; this is like their explanation of «وأرجُلَكُمْ» in the accusative as conjoined to the position of {برؤوسكم} [al-Māʾida: 6]; and because {يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ} is equivalent to "they wear bracelets", so this was construed on it. Third: that it is conjoined to «أساور», because «مِنْ» is redundant in it, as has been established. Fourth: that it is conjoined to that omitted object, the implied form being: "they are adorned therein with what is worn of bracelets, and pearls"; so «لؤلؤاً» is conjoined to «الملبوس» ("what is worn").
As for the genitive, it is on two views. First: conjoining it to «أساور». Second: conjoining it to «مِنْ ذهبٍ», because the bracelet is also made of pearls, strung one to another. Abū al-Baqāʾ forbade conjunction to «ذهب»; he said: "because a bracelet is not usually made of pearls, though it may properly be an ornament."
People disagreed about the spelling of this word in the Imām [the master codex]: al-Aṣmaʿī transmitted that in the Imām it is «لؤلؤ» without an alif after the wāw, and al-Jaḥdarī transmitted that it is present in the Imām after the wāw. This very disagreement, in reading and justification, applies to the word in Fāṭir as well.
Abū Bakr, in the narration of al-Muʿallā ibn Manṣūr from him, read «لؤلوا» with a hamza first and a wāw last; and in the narration of Yaḥyā from him, the reverse of that.
Al-Fayyāḍ read «ولُوْلِيا» with a wāw first and a yāʾ last. The original is «لُؤْلُؤاً»; he changed the two hamzas into two wāws, so there remained at the end of the noun a wāw after a ḍamma, and with it was done what was done with «أَدْلٍ», the plural of «دَلْو»: the wāw was changed into a yāʾ and the ḍamma into a kasra.
Ibn ʿAbbās read «وَلِيْلِيا» with two yāʾs: he did what al-Fayyāḍ did, then made the first wāw follow the second in the change. Ṭalḥa read «وَلُوْلٍ» in the genitive, conjoined to the genitive before it, as has preceded; the original is «ولُوْلُوٍ» with two wāws, then it underwent the same weak-letter change as «أَدْلٍ».
«اللُّؤْلُؤُ»: it has been said: large gems; and it has been said: small ones.

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {مِنَ القول}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الطيِّب», or a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in it. «مِنْ» is partitive or explicative (bayān).

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {وَيَصُدُّونَ}: there are three views on it. First: that it is conjoined to what precedes it. In that case, regarding its conjunction to the past verb, there are three interpretations. First: that the imperfect is used [here] not to indicate a specific time, present or future; rather only bare continuity is meant by it. Similar to it is {الذين آمَنُواْ وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ الله} [al-Raʿd: 28]. [Translator's note: the source reads «أنَّ المضارعَ قولاً يُقْصَدُ به», which appears to be corrupted from «أنَّ المضارعَ لا يُقْصَدُ به»; it is translated according to the evident sense.] Second: that it is interpreted as a past because of its conjunction to the past. Third: that it is in its proper sense, and the past before it is interpreted as future.
The second view: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «كفروا»; Abū al-Baqāʾ began with this. It is evidently corrupt, because it is an affirmative imperfect, and the wāw does not come before such a verb; what has occurred of that, rare as it is, is interpreted [otherwise], so the Qurʾān is not construed on it. On these two views the khabar (predicate) is omitted. They disagreed about where to estimate it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya estimated it after His saying «والبادِ», i.e. "those who disbelieved have lost", or "perished", and the like. Al-Zamakhsharī estimated it after His saying {والمسجد الحرام}, i.e. "those who disbelieved, We shall make them taste a painful punishment"; he estimated it so only because His saying {نُّذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ} indicates it.
However, the Shaykh said of al-Zamakhsharī's estimate after «المسجد الحرام»: "It is not correct", and he said: "because «الذي» is an adjective of «المسجد الحرام», so the place of the estimate is after «البادِ»." He means: his estimate entails separating the adjective from the qualified noun by an extraneous element, namely the khabar of «إنّ», so the construction becomes: "Those who disbelieved and bar from the path of Allah and the Sacred Mosque — We shall make them taste a painful punishment — which We made for the people." Al-Zamakhsharī can escape this objection by [saying]: we do not grant that «الذي جَعَلْناه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «المسجد» so that what he mentioned would follow; rather we make it cut off (maqṭūʿ) from it, in the accusative or the nominative.
Then the Shaykh said: "But al-Zamakhsharī's estimate is better than Ibn ʿAṭiyya's, because the conditional clause after it indicates it from the point of view of wording, whereas Ibn ʿAṭiyya looked at it from the point of view of meaning, because whoever is made to taste the punishment has lost and perished."
The third view: that the wāw in «ويَصُدُّون» is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar of «إنَّ», the implied form being: «إنَّ الذين كفروا يَصُدُّون». The redundancy of the wāw is a Kufan doctrine whose invalidity has preceded. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This corrupts the intended meaning." I say: I do not know from what angle the meaning is corrupted. Do you not see that if we said explicitly «إنَّ الذين كفروا يَصُدُّون», there would be no corruption of meaning in it? The impediment is only a technical one according to the people of Basra, not one of meaning — unless he intends a particular meaning that is corrupted by this estimate, in which case it would need to be explained.
His saying: {الذي جَعَلْنَاهُ}: it may be genitive as a naʿt, a badal (substitute) or an explicative apposition (bayān); accusative by an implied verb; or nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). «جَعَلَ» may be transitive to two objects in the sense of «صَيَّر» ("made into"), or transitive to one.
The majority read «سواءٌ» in the nominative. Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read it in the accusative here and in al-Jāthiya: {سَوَآءً مَّحْيَاهُمْ} [verse 21]; the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] agreed with him on the one in al-Jāthiya, and its justification will come. As for the nominative reading: if we say that «جَعَلَ» is in the sense of «صَيَّر», there are several views on the second object. First, and it is the most apparent: that the clause {سَوَآءٌ العاكف فِيهِ} is the second object. Then the best [analysis] of the nominative «سواءٌ» is that it is a fronted khabar, and «العاكف» and «البادي» a postponed mubtadaʾ. The khabar is singular even though the mubtadaʾ is two only because «سواء» is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description; this has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. Some allowed «سواءٌ» to be the mubtadaʾ and what follows it the khabar. That is weak or not allowed, in terms of beginning with an indefinite noun without a justification, and because whenever a definite and an indefinite come together, the definite is made the mubtadaʾ. On this view — I mean the clause being a second object — two views are possible regarding His saying «للناس». First: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the making, i.e. "We made it so for the sake of the people". Second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from the object of «جَعَلْناه»; Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned nothing else on this view, and its meaning is not clear.
The second view: that «للناس» is the second object, and the clause {سَوَآءٌ العاكف} is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, either from the relative noun or from its returning pronoun. Abū al-Baqāʾ began with this view. It is open to question, because it makes this clause, which is the point on which the benefit [of the statement] rests, a mere complement (faḍla).
The third view: that the second object is omitted. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The meaning: which We made for the people a qibla and a place of worship." This estimate of Ibn ʿAṭiyya points to this view. However, the Shaykh said: "There is no need for this estimate — unless he meant to explain the meaning, not the iʿrāb, in which case it is acceptable — because the clause is in the place of the second object, so there is no need for this estimate." If we make it transitive to one object, His saying «للناس» is attached to the making by way of cause. Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed two other views on it. First: that it is a ḥāl from the object of «جَعَلْناه». Second: that it is an object to which [the verb] is made transitive by the preposition. This second is not intelligible: how can «للناس» be an object to which the verb is made transitive by the preposition? This is something unintelligible. If he meant that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), it is an expression far from the grammarians' terminology.
As for the reading of Ḥafṣ: if we say «جَعَلَ» is transitive to two objects, «سواءً» is the second object; and if we say it is transitive to one, it is a ḥāl from the hāʾ of «جَعَلْناه». On both estimates «العاكف» is nominative by it as its agent, because it is a maṣdar used as a description, so it is equivalent to a derived active participle, the implied form being: "We made it, the resident being equal in it." This is indicated by their saying «مررتُ برجلٍ سواءٍ هو والعَدَمُ» ("I passed by a man to whom he and nothingness are equal"): «هو» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun latent in it, and «العَدَمُ» is conjoined to the latent pronoun, and for that reason it is nominative.
It is also narrated «سواءٍ والعدمُ» without emphasis, and that is anomalous (shādhdh).
Al-Aʿmash and a group read «سَواءً» in the accusative and «العاكفِ» in the genitive. There are two views on it. First: that it is a badal from «الناس», a badal of detailing (badal tafṣīl). Second: that it is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); this is what Ibn ʿAṭiyya meant by his saying "conjoined to «الناس»". In this reading the nominative of «سواء» is impossible, because it is corrupt in grammar and meaning; for that reason Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "and «سواءً» on this [reading] is accusative and nothing else."
Ibn Kathīr retained the yāʾ of «والبادي» in continuous recitation and in pause; Abū ʿAmr and Warsh retained it in continuous recitation and dropped it in pause; the rest dropped it in continuous recitation and in pause, and it is omitted in the Imām [the master codex].
His saying: {وَمَن يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ}: there are four views on it. First: that the object of «يُرِدْ» is omitted, and His saying «بإلحادٍ بظلم» are two consecutive (mutarādifa) ḥāls. The implied form: "and whoever intends in it anything whatsoever, deviating from the right course, doing wrong — We shall make him taste a painful punishment." It was omitted only so that it includes everything that may be included. Al-Zamakhsharī said its meaning. Second: that the object is likewise omitted, its implied form being "and whoever intends in it transgression", with «بإلحادٍ» a ḥāl, i.e. "bound up with deviation", and «بظُلْمٍ» a badal with the preposition repeated. Third: that «بظلمٍ» is attached to «يُرِدْ», the bāʾ being causal, i.e. "because of wrongdoing", and «بإلحاد» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), with the bāʾ redundant in it, as in His saying {وَلاَ تُلْقُواْ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ} [al-Baqara: 195] [and the saying]:
3380 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . لا يَقْرَأْنَ بالسُّوَر
(… they do not recite the sūras)
Abū ʿUbayda went to this, and recited [the verse] of al-Aʿshā:
3381 - ضَمِنَتْ برزقِ عيالِنا أرماحُنا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Our spears guaranteed the sustenance of our dependants …)
i.e. «ضَمِنَتْ رزقَ». This is supported by the reading of al-Ḥasan: «ومَنْ يُرِدْ إلحادهُ بظُلْمٍ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He meant «إلحاده فيه» (his deviating in it), and annexed it by widening the use of the adverb of place, like {مَكْرُ اليل} [Sabaʾ: 33]; its meaning: and whoever intends to deviate in it, doing wrong." Fourth: that «يُرِدْ» is made to include (taḍmīn) the sense of «يتلبَّس» ("to become involved in"), and for that reason it is made transitive with the bāʾ, i.e. "and whoever becomes involved in deviation, intending it".
The majority read «يُرِدْ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, from «الإرادة» (intending). Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ reported that it was read «يَرِدْ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "From «الوُرُود» (arriving), and its meaning: whoever comes in it with deviation, doing wrong."

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا}: i.e. "remember when". On the lām in «لإِبراهيم» there are three views. First: that it is for reason (ʿilla), and the object of «بَوَّأْنا» is omitted, i.e. "We settled people, for the sake of Ibrāhīm, at the site of the House". «بَوَّأَ» has come as explicitly transitive; the Exalted said: {وَلَقَدْ بَوَّأْنَا بني إِسْرَائِيلَ} [Yūnus: 93], {لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ مِّنَ الجنة غُرَفَاً} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 58]; and the poet said:
3382 - كَمْ مِنْ أَخٍ ليَ صالحٍ ... بَوَّأْتُه بيَديَّ لَحْدا
(How many a good brother of mine have I laid down with my own hands in a grave)
Second: that it is redundant (zāʾida) in the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). This is weak, for what you know: it is not added unless the governed word comes first or the governor is secondary (farʿ). Third: that it makes the verb transitive, on the basis that it is made to include (taḍmīn) the sense of a verb that is made transitive by it, i.e. "We prepared for him the site of the House", as you say "I prepared a house for him"; so the lām makes [the verb] transitive. Abū al-Baqāʾ said its meaning. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And remember when We made for Ibrāhīm the site of the House a place of abode." So he explained the meaning, in that he made «بَوَّأْنا» include the sense of «جَعَلْنا», and he does not intend an explanation of the iʿrāb.
On {مَكَانَ البيت} there are two views. The more apparent of them: that it is a mafʿūl bihi. Second: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "that it is an adverb (ẓarf)." This is impossible, in that it is a specific adverb of place, so properly it is made transitive to with «في».
His saying: {أَن لاَّ تُشْرِكْ}: on this «أنْ» there are three views [Translator's note: the source says three, but four are then listed]. First: that it is the explicative (mufassira) «أنْ». Al-Zamakhsharī said, after mentioning this view: "If you say: how can the prohibition of shirk and the command to purify the House be an explanation of the settling? I say: the settling was intended for the sake of worship, so it is as though it were said: We charged Ibrāhīm with worship; We said to him: do not associate." I say: Abū al-Qāsim [al-Zamakhsharī] means that the explicative «أنْ» must be preceded by what has the meaning of saying but not its letters, and nothing preceded except the settling, which does not mean saying, so he made it include the sense of saying. By his saying "We said: do not associate" he does not intend an explanation of the iʿrāb, but an explanation of the meaning, because the explicative «أنْ» does not explain explicit saying. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Its implied form is: saying to him, do not associate; so «أنْ» explains the implied saying." And this . . . . [Translator's note: there is a gap in the source here.]
Second: that it is lightened from the heavy [«أنَّ»]; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. It is open to question in that the lightened «أَنْ» must be preceded by a verb of certainty or of preponderance, as is its condition when it is doubled.
Third: that it is the maṣdar-forming «أنْ» which puts the imperfect in the accusative; it can be connected to the past, the imperfect and the imperative, and the prohibition is like the imperative. On this view «أنْ» is genitive by an implied lām of reason, i.e. "We settled him so that you do not associate". On this view the wording ought properly to have been «أن لا يشرك» with the third-person yāʾ, and it has been read so. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "That is strengthened by the reading of whoever read it with yāʾ", meaning the lower-dotted one. I say: the justification of the majority reading on this explanation is that it is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person to the second person.
Fourth: that it is the [maṣdar-forming] accusative-governing «أنْ», likewise made genitive by a lām, except that the lām is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "We did that so that you do not associate", making the prohibition its ṣila. The yāʾ reading strengthened that; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The default is that there is no implied element when there is no need for it.
ʿIkrima and Abū Nahīk read «أن لا يُشرِك» with yāʾ. The Shaykh said: "In the sense: that he should say the meaning of the saying that was said to him." Abū Ḥātim said: "On this reading the kāf must be in the accusative, in the sense of «لئلا تشركَ»." I say: it seems it was not evident to him that the maṣdar-forming «أنْ» can have a prohibitive clause as its ṣila, so he made «لا» negating and made «أنْ» govern the imperfect after it, so that it became a reason for the verb before it. This is not necessary, given what you have seen of the clarity of the meaning when it is made prohibitive.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying: {وَأَذِّن}: the majority read it with the dhāl doubled, in the sense of "call out". Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «آذِنْ» with the long vowel and the unstressed [dhāl], in the sense of "announce/inform". His saying {فِي الناس} makes this unlikely, since it ought then to be transitive by itself. According to what Abū al-Fatḥ transmitted from them, they also read «أَذِنَ» with the short vowel and the unstressed dhāl. Abū al-Fatḥ and the author of al-Lawāmiḥ explained it as conjoined to «بَوَّأنا», i.e. "and remember when We settled … and when He proclaimed among the people", and this is a clear explanation. The author of al-Lawāmiḥ added: "So there is a fronting and postponing in the speech, and «يأتوك» becomes jussive as the reply to the command in «وطهِّرْ»." Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributed a misreading of the script (taṣḥīf) to Abū al-Fatḥ in this reading, for after relating the reading of al-Ḥasan and Ibn Muḥayṣin «وآذِنْ» with the long vowel, he said: "This was misread by Ibn Jinnī, for he related from them «وأَذِنَ» as a past verb, and parsed it accordingly by making it conjoined to «بَوَّأْنا»."
I say: his work was not misread; rather that reading was related from them by Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī in his al-Lawāmiḥ, and Ibn Khālawayh also mentioned it. But he [Ibn ʿAṭiyya] had not come across it, so he attributed misreading to the one who had; had he taken his time, he would have been right, or nearly so.
Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «بالحِجِّ» with kasra on the ḥāʾ wherever it occurs, as I reported from him previously.
His saying: {رِجَالاً}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is the plural of «راجِل» ("on foot"), like «صاحِب» and «صِحاب», «تاجِر» and «تِجار», «قائِم» and «قِيام». ʿIkrima, al-Ḥasan and Abū Mijlaz read «رُجَّالاً» with ḍamma on the rāʾ and the jīm doubled; the unstressed form is also narrated from them. Ibn Abī Isḥāq agreed with them on the unstressed form, and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad [Translator's note: the source has «جعفر من محمد», evidently for «جعفر بن محمد»] and Mujāhid on the doubled form. It is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās with the alif. The unstressed form is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) like «ظُؤَار», and the doubled form is a broken plural like «صائم» and «صُوَّام». It is also narrated from ʿIkrima: «رُجَالى» like «نُعامى», with the feminine alif; and likewise from Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAṭāʾ, except that they doubled the jīm.
His saying: {وعلى كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ}: conjoined to «رِجالاً», so it is a ḥāl, i.e. "on foot and riding".
His saying: {يَأْتِينَ}: the nūn is the pronoun of «كلِّ ضامِرٍ», construed according to meaning, since the meaning is "on lean mounts". «يَأْتِيْنَ» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «ضامِر», and the plural pronoun was brought by construction according to meaning. It had been established at the beginning of this work that «كل», when annexed to an indefinite noun, its meaning is not taken into account except rarely, as in the saying:
3383 - جادَتْ عليه كلُّ عَيْنٍ ثَرَّةٍ ... فتركْنَ كلَّ حَديقةٍ كالدِّرْهَمِ
(Every abundant rain-cloud poured generously upon it, and they left every garden [round and bright] like a dirham)
This verse refutes that, for «كل» in it is annexed to an indefinite noun and its meaning has been taken into account. Someone had answered regarding the line of Zuhayr that it was permissible only because it is in two sentences, so I said: this verse is a single sentence, because «يَأْتِيْنَ» is a ṣifa of «ضامِر».
The Shaykh allowed the pronoun to include both «رجالاً» and «كل ضامر»; he said: "in the sense of groups and companies." I say: on this view it would be permissible, according to him, to say «الرجال يَأْتِيْنَ» [with the feminine plural]. It does not help him that «كل ضامر» is combined here with «الرجال», so that one might say: that was permissible since there was combined with it something for which it is permissible — because that entails giving precedence (taghlīb) to the non-rational over the rational, which is forbidden.
Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «يَأْتُونَ», giving precedence to the rational males. On this [reading] it is possible that His saying {وعلى كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ} is likewise a ḥāl, and that «يَأْتُون» is resumptive, with {مِن كُلِّ فَجٍّ} attached to it, i.e. "they will come to you on foot and riding", then He said: "they come from every pass"; and it is possible that it [«وعلى كل ضامر»] is attached to His saying «يَأْتُون», i.e. "they come on every lean mount from every pass", «يَأْتُون» also being resumptive. It is not permissible for it to be a ṣifa of «رجالاً» and of «ضامِر» together, because the qualified nouns differ in case: one of them is accusative and the other genitive. If you said «رأيتُ زيداً ومررت بعمرٍو العاقِلَيْن» ("I saw Zayd and passed by ʿAmr, the two intelligent ones") as a naʿt, it would not be permissible, except as cut off (qaṭʿ). Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that, for he said: "And «يَأْتُون» has been read, as a ṣifa of the men and the riders", and that is rejected by what I have mentioned.
«الضَّامِرُ» is the emaciated; one says: . . . . [Translator's note: there is a gap in the source here.] «العميق» is what is far downward. One says «بئر عَميق» and «مَعِيق»; so it may be a metathesis (maqlūb), because it is less common than the first. He said:
