3384 - إذا الخيلُ جاءت مِنْ فِجاجٍ عميقةٍ ... يَمُدُّ بها في السيرِ أشعثُ شاحِبُ
(When the horses came from deep, distant passes, a dishevelled, pale rider urging them on in the journey)
One says «عَمِقَ» and «عَمُقَ», with kasra and ḍamma on the ʿayn, «عَمْقاً» with fatḥa on the fāʾ [i.e. the first radical]. Al-Layth said: "«عَميق» and «مَعِيق», and «العَميق» is more frequent for a road." Al-Farrāʾ said: "«عميق» is the dialect of the Ḥijāz, and «مَعِيْق» the dialect of Tamīm." [One says] «أَعْمَقْتُ البئرَ» and «أَمْعَقْتُها», and «عَمُقَتْ» and «مَعُقَتْ», «عَماقَةً» and «مَعَاقة», «إعْماقاً» and «إمْعاقاً». Ruʾba said:
3385 - وقاتمِ الأعماقِ خاوي المُخْتَرَقْ ...
(And many a dusty-depthed [desert], its pathways empty …)
«الأعماق» here, with fatḥa on the hamza, is the plural of «عُمْق». On this there is no metathesis in «مَعِيق», because it is an independent dialectal form, and that is also the apparent sense of al-Layth's saying. Ibn Masʿūd read «فج مَعِيق» with the mīm first. One also says «غَمِيق» with the dotted ghayn.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {لِّيَشْهَدُواْ}: two views are possible regarding this lām. First: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «أَذِّن», i.e. "proclaim, that they may witness". Second: that it is attached to «يأْتُوْك», and this is the more apparent. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He made «منافع» indefinite because He meant benefits specific to this act of worship, religious and worldly, which are not found in other acts of worship."

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ لْيَقْضُواْ}: the majority read with kasra on the lām, which is the lām of command. Nāfiʿ, the Kufans and al-Bazzī read it with sukūn, treating the separate [word] like the connected, as in «كَتْف» [for «كَتِف»]. It is parallel to making the hāʾ of «هو» quiescent after «ثُمَّ» in the reading of al-Kisāʾī and Qālūn, where «ثُمَّ» is treated like wāw and fāʾ.
«التَّفَثُ»: it has been said that its origin is «التَّفّ», which is the dirt of the nails, the fāʾ being changed into a thāʾ, as in «مُغْثُور» for «مُغْفُور». It has also been said: it is dirt and filth; one says «ما تَفَثُكَ؟» ("what is your filth?"). Quṭrub reported: «تَفِثَ الرجلُ», i.e. his dirt increased on his journey. The meaning of «ليقْضُوا تَفَثَهم» is: let them do what the one in iḥrām does, removing hair, dishevelment and the like, upon leaving iḥrām; and included in this is the completion of all the rites, since this is not done except after performing all the rites.
His saying: {وَلْيُوفُواْ}: Abū Bakr read «وليُوَفُّوا» with doubling, and the rest with the unstressed form. It has preceded in al-Baqara that there are three dialectal forms: «وَفَى», «وفَّى» and «أوفى». Ibn Dhakwān read «ولِيُوْفوا» with kasra on the lām, and the rest with sukūn; the same disagreement applies to His saying {وَلْيَطَّوَّفُواْ}.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {ذلك}: the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter and the case is that". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Just as a writer puts forward a part of his letter on some topics, then, when he wishes to embark on another topic, says: "This [being so]; and such-and-such had happened."" Ibn ʿAṭiyya estimated it: "your obligation is that", or "what is required is that". It has also been said: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "that is the matter which I have mentioned". It has also been said: it is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "comply with that". The parallel of this demonstrative is the saying of Zuhayr after preceding sentences describing Harim ibn Sinān:
3386 - هذا وليس كمَنْ يَعْيا بخُطْبَتِه ... وسَطَ النَّدِيِّ إذا ما ناطقٌ نَطَقا
(This [being so] — and he is not like one who falters in his speech amid the assembly when a speaker speaks)
His saying «فهو»: «هو» is the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun) understood from His saying {وَمَن يُعَظِّمْ}, i.e. "his honouring of the sacred things of Allah is better for him", like His saying, exalted is He: {اعدلوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ} [al-Māʾida: 8]. «خيرٌ» here apparently is an elative, with the well-known interpretation.
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا يتلى عَلَيْكُمْ}: it may be a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), referred to what becomes forbidden of the grazing livestock because of an incidental cause, such as dying [of itself] and the like; or it may be a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), since there is nothing forbidden in them [per se]. The establishment of this view has preceded at the beginning of al-Māʾida.
His saying: {مِنَ الأوثان}: on «مِنْ» there are three views. First: that it is for clarifying the genus (bayān al-jins); this is the well-known view of the parsers, and it is paraphrased by your saying: "the filth which is the idols". It has preceded that this is the condition for its being explicative; and many places come in which neither that nor part of it is possible. Second: that it is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). Abū al-Baqāʾ mixed the two views and made them one, for he said: "«مِنْ» is for clarifying the genus, i.e. avoid the filth of this kind, and it is in the sense of beginning of extent here" — meaning that in meaning it amounts to that; but it does not amount to it at all. Third: that it is partitive (tabʿīḍ). Ibn ʿAṭiyya considered the one who said it was partitive to be in error, for he said: "Whoever said that «مِنْ» is partitive has inverted the meaning of the verse and corrupted it." Yet the partitive is possible in it, by meaning by «الرِّجْس» the worship of idols — Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Jurayj said this — so it is as though He said: "so avoid, of the idols, the filth, which is the worship", because what is forbidden regarding idols is only the worship. Do you not see that one can conceive of using an idol in building and other things whose use the Law has not forbidden? An idol has aspects, among them its being worshipped, which is one of its aspects. The Shaykh said this, and it is a far-fetched interpretation.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {حُنَفَآءَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «اجْتَنِبوا». Likewise {غَيْرَ مُشْرِكِينَ}, which is an emphasising ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), since their being ḥunafāʾ (upright in monotheism) entails their not associating.
His saying: {فَتَخْطَفُهُ}: Nāfiʿ read it with fatḥa on the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ doubled [«فَتَخَطَّفُه»]; its origin is «تَخْتَطِفُه», which was assimilated. The rest of the Seven read «فَتَخْطَفُه» with sukūn on the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ unstressed. Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash and Abū Rajāʾ read it with kasra on the tāʾ, the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ, with doubling. Also narrated from al-Ḥasan is fatḥa on the doubled ṭāʾ with kasra on the tāʾ and the khāʾ. It is narrated from al-Aʿmash like the majority reading, except without the fāʾ: «تَخْطَفُه». The justification of these readings has preceded in full near the beginning of al-Baqara, when I mentioned the readings in His saying, exalted is He, {يَكَادُ البرق يَخْطَفُ} [al-Baqara: 20], so I shall not repeat it.
Abū Jaʿfar read «الرياحُ» in the plural. His saying «خَرَّ» is in the sense of «يَخِرُّ» ("falls"); for that reason the future «فَتَخْطَفُهُ» was conjoined to it. It may also be in its proper sense, with «فَتَخْطَفُه» not conjoined to it but the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «فهو يَخْطَفُه» ("then [the birds are such that they] snatch him").
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This simile may be composite or separate. If it is a composite simile, it is as though He said: whoever associates [others] with Allah has destroyed himself with a destruction beyond which there is [no destruction], by depicting his state in the image of the state of one who has fallen from the sky and been snatched by the birds, so that he is dispersed in shreds in their crops, or [whom] the wind has buffeted until it hurled him down into some distant place of casting. If it is separate, He has likened faith, in its loftiness, to the sky; the one who abandoned faith and associated [others] with Allah to the one falling from the sky; the whims that divide his thoughts to the snatching birds; and the devil who hurls him into the valley of error to the wind which hurls what it buffets into some destructive abyss." I say: this expression of Abū al-Qāsim is among what spurs you to learn the science of rhetoric (ʿilm al-bayān), for it is of the utmost eloquence.
«الأَوْثان» is the plural of «وَثَن». «الوَثَنُ» is applied to what is fashioned of copper, iron or wood. It is also applied to the cross: "It is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he said to ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, having seen a cross on his neck: Throw this «الوثن» off you." Al-Aʿshā said:
3387 - يطوفُ العبادُ بأبوابِه ... كطَوْفِ النصارى ببَيْتِ الوَثَنْ
(The ʿIbād [tribesmen] circle about his gates as the Christians circle the house of the idol)
Its derivation is from «وَثَن الشيءُ», i.e. it stayed in its place and remained fixed, so it is «واثِنٌ». [A line of] Ruʾba was recited:
3388 - على أَخِلاَّء الصَّفاءِ الوُثَّنِ ...
(… upon the sincere friends who stay firm)
i.e. those who remain upon the covenant. The difference between «الوَثَن» and «الصنم» has preceded.
«السَّحيقُ» is the distant. From it is «سَحَقَه اللهُ», i.e. Allah put him far away; and his saying, upon him be peace: "Then I shall say: «سُحْقاً سُحْقاً»", i.e. "far away, far away". «النَّخْلة السَّحُوقُ», the palm tree stretching up into the sky, is from that.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {ذلك}: its iʿrāb is like the iʿrāb of the preceding «ذلك». The explanation of «الشَّعيرة» and its derivation have preceded in al-Māʾida.
His saying: {فَإِنَّهَا مِن تَقْوَى القلوب}: on this pronoun there are two views. First: that it is the pronoun of «الشعائر», on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "for honouring them is from the piety of hearts". Second: that it is the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun) understood from the verb before it, i.e. "for the honouring is from the piety of hearts". The pronoun referring back to the conditional noun from this apodosis clause is implied, its implied form being: "for it is from the piety of hearts, on their part". Those who allow «أل» to stand in place of the pronoun — they are the Kufans — allowed that here, the implied form being "from the piety of their hearts", like His saying {فَإِنَّ الجنة هِيَ المأوى} [al-Nāziʿāt: 41]; its establishment has preceded. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "I.e. honouring them is among the acts of those who possess piety of hearts; these muḍāfs were omitted, and the meaning is not sound except by estimating them, because there must be something referring back from the apodosis to «مَنْ» so that it is linked to it." The Shaykh said: "What he estimated is devoid of anything referring back from the apodosis to «مَنْ». Do you not see that in his saying "for honouring them is among the acts of those who possess piety of hearts" there is no pronoun anywhere referring back from the apodosis to «مَنْ» to link it? Its correction is to say: "for honouring them is [a part] of it [from him]", so the pronoun in «منه» refers back to «مَنْ»."
The majority read «القلوب» in the genitive. It has also been read in the nominative as the agent of the maṣdar before it, namely «تقوى».

semin-durr:33-33.t: [His saying: {فِيهَا}:] The pronoun in «فيها» refers back to «الشعائر» in the sense of the laws, i.e. "for you [there are benefits] in holding fast to them". It has also been said: it refers back to the grazing livestock (bahīmat al-anʿām).

semin-durr:34-34.t: His saying: {مَنسَكاً}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read this and the one after it «مَنْسِكاً» with kasra, and the rest with fatḥa. It has been said: they have one meaning, and what is meant by «المَنْسَك» is the place of the rite, or the maṣdar (verbal noun). It has also been said: the kasra form is a place, and the fatḥa form a maṣdar. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The kasra in this is anomalous (shādhdh), and analogy does not allow it; it seems likely that al-Kisāʾī heard it from the Arabs." I say: this statement of his is not acceptable. How can he say: "it seems likely that al-Kisāʾī heard it"? Al-Kisāʾī says: "I read it so"; so how would he need [to have] heard it [from the Arabs] while he holds to the strongest of hearings, namely his transmission of it as mutawātir Qurʾān? His saying "anomalous" means in terms of analogy, not usage, for it is eloquent in usage. That is because for faʿala yafʿulu, with ḍamma on the second radical in the imperfect, the analogy of its mafʿal form is that its second radical takes fatḥa absolutely, i.e. whether time, place or the maṣdar is meant. Some words have deviated, which the grammarians have recorded in their books, and I have also mentioned them in this work.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {الذين إِذَا ذُكِرَ الله وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ}: this relative noun may be in the position of the genitive, the accusative or the nominative. The genitive on three views: as naʿt (adjective) of «المُخْبِتِيْن», as a badal (substitute) from them, or as an explicative apposition (bayān) for them. The accusative is by way of praise (al-madḥ). The nominative is on an implied «هم», which is also praise; the grammarians call it "cutting off" (qaṭʿ).
His saying: {والمقيمي الصلاة}: the majority read «الصلاةِ» in the genitive, by annexation of «المقيمين» to it. Al-Ḥasan, and Abū ʿAmr in one narration, read it in the accusative, on the nūn being dropped for lightness, just as the tanwīn is dropped for the meeting of two quiescent letters. Ibn Masʿūd and al-Aʿmash read according to this original: «والمقيمينَ الصلاةَ», retaining the nūn, with «الصلاة» in the accusative. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «والمقيمَ الصلاةَ» with a mīm followed by nothing. This does not differ from the majority reading in pronunciation; its difference from it only appears in pause and in writing.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {والبدن}: the majority read «البُدْنَ» in the accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb with a pronoun). The accusative was preferred, even though it requires an implied [verb], over the nominative, which does not require it, because a verbal sentence precedes the ishtighāl sentence. It has also been read in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause after it being the khabar (predicate).
The majority also read with the dāl quiescent. Al-Ḥasan read it with ḍamma — and it is also narrated from Nāfiʿ and from Shayba [Translator's note: the source has «وشيخةِ أبي جعفر», most likely for «وشيبةَ وأبي جعفر», "Shayba and Abū Jaʿfar"] — and both are plurals of «بَدَنَة», like «ثَمَرة», «ثُمُر» and «ثُمْر». So the quiescent form may be a lightening of the ḍamma form, or it may be original. It has also been said: «البُدْن» and «البُدُن» are the plural of «بَدَن», and «البَدَن» is a plural of «بَدَنَة», like «خَشَبة» and «خَشَب»; then «خَشَب» is pluralised as «خُشُب» and «خُشْب». It has also been said: «البُدْن» is a singular noun, not a plural, meaning a generic noun (ism jins). Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «البُدُنَّ» with ḍamma on the bāʾ and the dāl and the nūn doubled. It admits two views. First: that he read like al-Ḥasan, then paused on the word and doubled its final radical, as in their saying «هذا فَرُخّْ», and then treated continuous recitation like pause in that respect. Second: it may be a noun on the pattern fuʿull, like «عُتُلّ».
The «بَدَنة» is called «بَدَنة» because it is fattened («تُبْدَن», i.e. «تُسَمَّن»). Is it specific to camels? The majority hold so. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«البُدْن» is the plural of «بَدَنَة», so called because of the bulk of its body (badan), and it is camels specifically. Because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ joined cattle to camels when he said: "The «بَدَنَة» is for seven, and the cow is for seven", making cattle take the ruling of camels, the «بَدَنة» came to include both kinds in the Law according to Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions; otherwise «البُدْن» are camels, and the verse indicates that." It has also been said that it is not specific. Al-Layth said: "«البَدَنَة» with the hāʾ applies to the she-camel, the cow, the camel and whatever is acceptable as an offering (hady) and a sacrifice, and does not apply to sheep." ʿAṭāʾ and others said: "whatever has been marked [as an offering] (ushʿira) of she-camels or cows." Others said: «البُدْن» means the aged among camels and cattle; and it is said of the fat among men; and it is a singular generic noun.
His saying: {مِّن شَعَائِرِ الله}: it is the second object of «الجَعْل» in the sense of «التصيير» ("making into").
His saying: {لَكُمْ فِيهَا خَيْرٌ}: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from «ها» of «جَعَلْناها» or from «شعائر الله». These two rest on whether the pronoun in «فيها» refers back to «البُدْن» or to «شعائر»; the first is the view of the majority.
His saying: {صَوَآفَّ}: accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "lined up, side by side". Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Zayd ibn Aslam read «صَوافي», the plural of «صافِيَة», i.e. "purely for the Face of Allah the Exalted". ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read it likewise, except that he gave the yāʾ tanwīn, reading «صَوافياً». This was found problematic in that it is an ultimate plural (jamʿ mutanāhī) [hence diptote]. It has been explained in two ways. First, which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned: that the tanwīn is a substitute for the letter of prolongation (ḥarf al-iṭlāq) in pause. He means that he paused on «صَوافي» by prolonging the fatḥa of the yāʾ, from which an alif arose called the letter of prolongation, and then substituted this tanwīn for it; this is what the grammarians call the tanwīn of trilling (tanwīn al-tarannum).
Second: that it came according to the dialect of those who make diptotes triptote.
Al-Ḥasan read «صَوافٍ» with kasra and tanwīn. Its justification: he made it accusative with an implied fatḥa, so the ruling of this word became like its ruling in the nominative and genitive, in dropping the yāʾ and substituting tanwīn, as in «هؤلاء جوارٍ» and «مررت بجوارٍ». Implying the fatḥa on the yāʾ is frequent, as in their saying «أعْطِ القوسَ بارِيْها» ("give the bow to the one who carves it"), and the saying:
3389 - كأنَّ أيْدِيهنَّ بالقاعِ القَرِقْ ... أيديْ جوارٍ يتعاطَيْنَ الوَرِق
(As though their forefeet on the smooth plain were the hands of slave-girls passing silver coins to one another)
and the saying:
3390 - وكَسَوْتُ عارٍ لَحْمُه . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And I clothed one whose flesh was bare …)
This is indicated by the reading of some «صَوافيْ» with a quiescent yāʾ and without tanwīn, as in «رأيتُ القاضيْ يا فتى» ("I saw the judge, young man") with the yāʾ quiescent. It is also possible that in this reading he made the yāʾ quiescent for pause and then treated continuous recitation like it.
The ʿAbādila [the ʿAbd Allāhs among the Companions], Mujāhid and al-Aʿmash read «صَوافِنْ» with nūn, the plural of «صَافِنَة», which is the one that stands on three [legs] and the tip of the fourth. However, that is used only of horses, as in His saying {الصافنات الجياد} [Ṣād: 31], which will come; so its use for camels is a metaphor (istiʿāra).
«الوجوبُ» is falling. «وجَبَتِ الشَمسُ», i.e. the sun set (fell); «وجَبَ الجِدَارُ», i.e. the wall fell. From it is the legal «الواجب» (obligation), as though it had fallen upon us and become binding on us. Aws ibn Ḥajar said:
3391 - ألم تُكْسَفِ الشمسُ شمسُ النَّها ... رِ والبدرُ للجبل الواجبِ
(Were not the sun — the sun of the day — and the full moon eclipsed for the fallen mountain [i.e. the great man who died]?)
His saying «القانِعَ والمعتَّر»: there are several views on them. «القانِعُ» is the one who asks, and «المُعْتَرُّ» the one who presents himself without asking. Some said the reverse. Ibn ʿAbbās said: «القانِعُ» is the one content with what you have given him, and «المعترُّ» the one who presents himself without asking. Also from him: «القانعُ» is the one who abstains [from asking], and «المعترُّ» the one who asks. Some said: «القانِعُ» is the one satisfied with a small thing, from «قَنِعَ يَقْنَعُ قَناعةً» so he is «قانِعٌ»; and «القَنِعُ» without alif is the one who asks — Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«القانِعُ» is the one who asks, from «قَنِعْتُ» and «كَنَعْتُ» when you humble yourself before him, and «سألتُه قُنُوْعاً» [I asked him humbly]; and «المُعْتَرُّ» is the one who presents himself without asking. Or «القانِعُ» is the one content with what he has and with what he is given, without asking, from «قَنِعْتُ قَنَعاً وقَناعة»; and «المعترُّ» is the one who presents himself by asking." End of quotation. Some distinguished the two meanings by the maṣdar (verbal noun), saying: «قَنِعَ يَقْنَع قُنوعاً», i.e. he asked; and «قَناعة», i.e. he abstained, making do with his bare sufficiency and being content with it. He recited [the verse] of al-Shammākh:
3392 - لَمالُ المَرْءِ يُصْلِحُه فيُغْني ... مَفاقِرَه أَعَفُّ من القُنوعِ
(A man's wealth, which he husbands so that it covers his needs, is more decent than begging)
Ibn Qutayba said: "«المُعْتَرُّ» is the one who presents himself without asking. One says «عَرَّه», «اعتَرَّه», «عَراه» and «اعْتراه», i.e. he came to him seeking his kindness." He said:
3393 - لَعَمْرُك ما المُعتَرُّ يَغْشى بلادَنا ... لِنَمْنَعَه بالضائعِ المُتَهَضِّمِ
(By your life, the needy visitor who comes to our land is not one whom we would refuse, to be left neglected and wronged)
And the saying of the other:
3394 - سَلي الطارِقَ المعترَّ يا أمَّ مالِكٍ ... إذا ما اعْتَراني بينَ قِدْري ومَجْزَري
(Ask the night-visitor in need, O Umm Mālik, [how I am] when he comes to me between my cooking-pot and my place of slaughter)
Abū Rajāʾ read «القَنِع» without alif. There are two views on it. First: that its original is «القانِع», and he dropped the alif, as they said «مِقْوَل», «مِخْيَط», «جَنَدِل» and «عُلَبِط» for «مِقْوال», «مِخْياط», «جَنَادل» and «عُلابط». Second: that «القانِع» is the one satisfied with little, and «القَنِع» is the one who asks, as has been established. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«القَنِعُ» is the one who is satisfied, nothing else."
Al-Ḥasan read «والمُعْتري», an active participle from «اعْتَرى يَعْتري». Ismāʿīl read — and it is also narrated from Abū Rajāʾ and al-Ḥasan — «والمُعْتَرِ» with kasra on the rāʾ, making do with the kasra in place of the final radical.
It has also been read «المُعْتَرِيَ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is in its meaning", i.e. in the meaning of «المعترّ» in the majority reading.
[His saying:] {كذلك سَخَّرْنَاهَا}: the kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar, or a ḥāl from that maṣdar.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
Likewise His saying: {كذلك سَخَّرَهَا}: and {لِتُكَبِّرُواْ} is attached to it (mutaʿalliq). {على مَا هَدَاكُمْ} is attached to the takbīr (magnifying); it was made transitive by «على» because it implies the meaning of thanksgiving.
His saying: {لَن يَنَالَ الله لُحُومُهَا}: The majority read both verbs with the yāʾ of the third person, because the feminine is figurative (majāzī) and there is a separation between them. It was also read with the tāʾ in both, taking the word's form into account. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «لحومَها ولا دماءَها» in the accusative, with the Majestic Name in the nominative, and «لكن يُنالُه» with a ḍamma on the yāʾ, so that the one standing in the place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil) is «التقوى»; and «منكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «التقوى», and it is also permissible that it be attached to «تَنالُه» itself.

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {يُدَافِعُ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «يَدْفَعُ», and the rest read «يُدافع». There are two views on it. One is that fāʿala has the sense of the simple form faʿala, as in jāwaztuhu and juztuhu, and sāfartu and ṭāraqtu. The second is that it was brought out on the pattern of mufāʿala for intensification, because the verb of mufāʿala is stronger than others. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «Difāʿ is fitting because there has arisen for the believers [one] who repels them and harms them, so resisting him and repelling him on their behalf comes as mudāfaʿa (mutual repelling)», meaning that the reciprocity (mufāʿala) is taken into account in it.

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ}: Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim read it in the passive; the rest read it in the active. As for «يُقاتِلون», Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read it in the passive, and the rest in the active. From the two verbs together it results that Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ made both passive; that Ibn Kathīr, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī made both active; that Abū ʿAmr and Abū Bakr made the first passive and the second active; and that Ibn ʿĀmir did the reverse of this. So there are four categories. What permission was given for is omitted because it is known, that is: for those who are fought, to fight. And {بِأَنَّهُمْ ظُلِمُواْ} is attached to «أُذِنَ», and the bāʾ is causal, that is: because they have been wronged.

semin-durr:41-41.t: His saying: {الذين إِنْ مَّكَّنَّاهُمْ}: What was permissible for the relative noun before it is permissible for this relative noun, and this one adds to it that it may be a badal (substitute) from «مَنْ يَنْصُرُه»; al-Zajjāj mentioned it, that is: "and Allah will surely help the one whom, if We establish them…". And «إنْ مَكَّنَّاهم» is the protasis (sharṭ), and «أقاموا» is its apodosis (jawāb), and the whole conditional sentence is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.

semin-durr:44-44.t: His saying: {نَكِيرِ}: nakīr is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning inkār (denunciation), like nadhīr meaning indhār (warning). Warsh kept the yāʾ of «نَكيري» wherever it occurs in connected recitation, and dropped it in pause. The rest drop it both in connected recitation and in pause.

semin-durr:47-47.t: His saying: {مِّمَّا تَعُدُّونَ}: The two (al-Akhawān, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ibn Kathīr read «يَعُدُّون» with the yāʾ of the third person. The rest read it with the tāʾ of address; both are clear.

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {وَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ}: Its like has already been discussed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: why was the first conjoined with the fāʾ and this one with the wāw? I say: the first came as a substitute (badal) for His saying {فَكَيْفَ كَانَ نَكِيرِ}, whereas [as for] this one, its rule is the rule of the two sentences before it, conjoined with the wāw, I mean His saying {وَلَن يُخْلِفَ الله وَعْدَهُ وَإِنَّ يَوْماً عِندَ رَبِّكَ كَأَلْفِ سَنَةٍ}.
[Translator's note: the source text leaves al-Zamakhsharī's quotation without a closing mark.]

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying: {مُعَاجِزِينَ}: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read it with shaddah on the jīm here and in the two places in Sabaʾ; the rest read «مُعاجزين» in all three places. Al-Jaḥdarī, in the whole Quran, is like the reading of Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr; and Ibn al-Zubayr read «مُعْجِزين» with sukūn on the ʿayn.
As for the first, there are two views on it. One, al-Fārisī said: its meaning is "ascribing the Companions of the Prophet, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to incapacity", like fassaqtuhu, that is, you ascribed him to wickedness. The second is that it is for intensification, and its meaning is "dissuading people from faith". As for the second, its meaning is "supposing that they can render us incapable". It was also said: "being obstinate". Al-Zamakhsharī said: «ʿĀjazahu means sābaqahu (he raced him), because each of the two is seeking to make the other incapable of catching up with him. When he outstrips him it is said: aʿjazahu and ʿajazahu. So the meaning is: those who race, or are racing, in their claim and estimation, hoping that their scheming against Islam will succeed for them. The meaning is: they strove in its meaning with corruption.» Abū l-Baqāʾ said: muʿājizīn has the meaning of the doubled form, like ʿāhada and ʿahhada. It was also said: ʿājaza means sābaqa, and ʿajaza means sabaqa.
[Translator's note: the source text has unbalanced quotation marks in this entry; they are rendered here as the sense requires.]

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ إِذَا تمنى أَلْقَى الشيطان}: There are three views on this sentence after «إلاَّ». The first: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رسول», the meaning being: "We did not send him except that his state was this", the ḥāl being restricted. The second: that it is in the position of an adjective (ṣifa) of «رسول», so its position may be judged genitive with regard to the form of the qualified noun, and accusative with regard to its position, since «مِنْ» is redundant in it. The third: that it is in the position of an exception from other than the same kind; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it, meaning that it is a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).
And this «إذا» may be conditional, which is the apparent sense and which al-Ḥawfī held, and may be merely temporal. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: «They stated explicitly that what follows it in the negative, meaning after «إلاَّ», is the imperfect without condition, as in mā Zaydun illā yafʿalu and mā raʾaytu Zaydan illā yafʿalu; and the past, on condition that a verb precedes, as in {مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلاَّ كَانُواْ} [Yā Sīn: 30], or that qad accompanies it, as in mā Zaydun illā qad faʿala. What comes after «إلاَّ» in the verse is a conditional sentence, and no past verb accompanied by «قَدْ» follows it, nor one bare of it. If what they stated is sound, it is interpreted as meaning that «إذا» was stripped to mere temporality with no condition in it, and was inserted between «إلاَّ» and the verb «أَلْقى», which is a permissible separation; so «إلاَّ» is, in the implied sense, followed by a past verb and its condition is met, namely that a verb precedes «إلاَّ», which is «وما أَرْسَلْنا».»
I (al-Samīn) say: There is no need for this strain, which takes the verse out of its meaning. Rather it is a conditional sentence, either a ḥāl, or a ṣifa, or an exception, as in His saying {إِلاَّ مَن تولى وَكَفَرَ فَيُعَذِّبُهُ} [al-Ghāshiya: 23]. How can separation by it and by the verb after it between «إلاَّ» and «ألقى» be claimed, with no necessity calling for it and with the meaning not being sound?
And His saying, the Exalted: {إِذَا تمنى}: the pronoun was put in the singular, although two things precede it, one conjoined to the other with the wāw, because the speech contains an omission, its implied form being: "We did not send before you any messenger except when he wished, nor any prophet except when he wished", like His saying {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [al-Tawba: 62]. The omission is either from the first or from the second.
As for the pronoun in «أُمْنِيَّتِه», there are two views on it. One, which is the one that ought to be held, is that it refers to the Devil (al-Shayṭān). The second is that it refers to the Messenger; and they transmitted commentaries on that, of whose soundness Allah knows best.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying: {لِّيَجْعَلَ}: There are three views on what this lām is attached to. The most apparent is that it is attached to «يُحْكِم», that is: "Allah makes His signs firm so that He may make…", and His saying {والله عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ} is a parenthetical sentence; al-Ḥawfī inclined to this. The second: that it is attached to «يَنْسَخُ»; Ibn ʿAṭiyya inclined to this, and it is also apparent. The third: that it is attached to «ألقى», which is not apparent. There are two views on the lām: one, that it is of cause; the other, that it is of consequence. As for «ما» in His saying {مَا يُلْقِي}, the apparent is that it has the meaning of "that which" (alladhī), and it may be maṣdarī (forming a verbal noun).
His saying: {والقاسية}: the «al» in «القاسية» is a relative, and the adjective is its ṣila (relative clause); «قلوبُهم» is its agent (fāʿil), and the pronoun annexed to it is the referent returning to the relative. The ṣila was made feminine because its nominative is a figurative feminine; had a verb been put in its place, its being feminine would be permissible. «القاسيةِ» is conjoined to «الذين», that is: "a trial for those in whose hearts is a sickness and a trial for those whose hearts are hardened".
His saying: {وَإِنَّ الظالمين} is an instance of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, since the original is «وإنهم في ضلال», but they were made explicit as overt nouns in order to testify against them with this blameworthy description.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying: {وَلِيَعْلَمَ الذين}: it is conjoined to «ليجعلَ», the conjoining of a cause to a like cause. As for the pronoun in «أنَّه», there are two views. One, which al-Zamakhsharī held, is that it refers to the Devil's being given power, that is: "so that the believers may know that the Devil's being given power is the truth". The second, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya inclined to, is that it refers to the Quran. Although no mention of it has preceded, it is in the force of what is uttered.
His saying: {فَيُؤْمِنُواْ} is conjoined to «وليعلمَ», and «فَتُخْبِتَ» is conjoined to it. How beautifully these fāʾs have fallen into place!
The majority read «لهادِيْ الذين» with annexation (iḍāfa), for lightness. Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Abū Ḥaywa read the adjective with tanwīn, making it govern the relative noun.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
Both al-miriya and al-muriya, with kasra and with ḍamma, are well-known dialectal forms. The apparent sense of Abū l-Baqāʾ's words is that they are two readings, but I do not remember the ḍamma here. As for the pronoun in «منه», it was said that it refers to the Quran; it was said, to the Messenger; and it was said, to what the Devil cast.
His saying: {عَقِيمٍ}: ʿaqīm is from ʿuqm (barrenness). There are two views on it. One is that it means blocking; one says "a woman maʿqūmat al-raḥim", that is, her womb is blocked from giving birth. This is the statement of Abū ʿUbayd. The second is that its root is cutting off. From it comes «al-mulk ʿaqīm» (kingship is barren), that is, because it cuts the tie of kinship through the competition for it. From it also comes the barren woman, because her childbearing is cut off. And ʿuqm is the cutting off of good, and from it «a barren day» (yawm ʿaqīm). It was said: because there is no night after it and no day, so it was likened to one whose offspring has been cut off. This is if the Day of Resurrection is meant by it. If the Day of Badr is meant, it was said: because the sons of war are killed in it, so it is as though the women had not borne them, and so they become barren. One says: a ʿaqīm man and a ʿaqīma woman, that is, those to whom no child is born; and the plural is ʿuqum.
[Translator's note: this entry begins without a «قوله» heading in the source; it opens with a comment on {مِرْيَةٍ}.]

semin-durr:56-56.t: His saying: {يَوْمَئِذٍ}: it is accusative through the sense of being established (istiqrār) implied in «لله», because it occurs as a predicate (khabar). And «يَحْكم» may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the name Allah, and may be resumptive. The tanwīn in «يومئذٍ» is a replacement for a sentence, which al-Zamakhsharī estimated as «the day they believe», and it is necessary for the disappearance of doubt (miriya). He also estimated it as «the day their doubt disappears».

semin-durr:57-57.t: His saying: {والذين كَفَرُواْ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject). And His saying {فأولئك} and what follows it is its khabar (predicate). The fāʾ entered because, as you know, the mubtadaʾ implies the meaning of a condition with the stated condition. As for «لهم», it may be a khabar of «أولئك», with «عذاب» an agent (fāʿil) of it because it relies on the one reported about; or it may be a fronted khabar, with what follows it a mubtadaʾ and the sentence a khabar of «أولئك».

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {لَيَرْزُقَنَّهُمُ}: the answer to an omitted oath (qasam). The oath sentence and its answer are the khabar of His saying {والذين هَاجَرُواْ}, and in it is evidence for an oath sentence occurring as a khabar of a mubtadaʾ. Whoever forbids this supplies an implied "saying" which is the khabar, by which this oath sentence is quoted; that is the weaker view.
His saying: {رِزْقاً}: it may be a second object (mafʿūl), on the basis that it is of the type of al-riʿy and al-dhibḥ, that is: "a good provision, something provided"; and it may be an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun). As for His saying {ثُمَّ قتلوا} and His saying «مُدْخَلاً», the disagreement about the reading of both has already been given in Āl ʿImrān and in al-Nisāʾ.

semin-durr:59-59.t: The sentence «لَيُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ» may be a badal (substitute) from «لَيَرْزُقَنَّهم», and may be resumptive.

semin-durr:60-60.t: His saying: {ذلك}: the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "the matter is that". What follows it is resumptive. The bāʾ in His saying {بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبَ بِهِ} is causal in both places; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it. [Translator's note: the next sentence is garbled in the source («الذين يظهر أن الأُولى يُشبه أن تكونَ للآله»); it appears to say that it seems the first is likely to be of instrumentality, reading «للآلة» for «للآله».] And {وَمَنْ عَاقَبَ} is a mubtadaʾ, its khabar being {لَيَنصُرَنَّهُ الله}.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {ذلك}: a mubtadaʾ, and {بِأَنَّ الله} is its khabar, that is: "that help is because Allah makes the night enter…".
The majority read «وأنَّ ما» as conjoined to the first; al-Ḥasan read it with kasra as a resumption.

semin-durr:62-62.t:
His saying: {هُوَ الحق}: it may be a fasl (separating pronoun) and a mubtadaʾ. Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed that it be tawkīd (emphasis), and began with it. That is a mistake, because a pronoun does not give emphasis to an overt noun, and the accusative form would have been more fitting for it than the nominative, so one would say «iyyāhu», because the antecedent is accusative.
Al-Akhawān, Ḥafṣ and Abū ʿAmr read «يَدْعُون» here and in Luqmān with the yāʾ (of the third person); the rest read it with the tāʾ (of address). The verb is active. Mujāhid and al-Yamānī read it with the yāʾ, in the passive. The wāw which is a pronoun refers to «ما» according to its meaning, and what is meant by it is the idols or the devils.
[Translator's note: «الأخَوان» (al-Akhawān) is understood as Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, as elsewhere in this book.]

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying: {فَتُصْبِحُ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is imperfect in form but past in meaning, its implied form being «فأصبحتْ», so it is conjoined to «أَنْزَل»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it. Then, after making it conjoined to «أَنْزل», he said: «so it has no position then.» That is a self-contradictory statement, because conjoining it to «أَنْزَلَ» requires that it have a position in the i'rab, namely the nominative as the khabar of «أنَّ», but that is not permissible for lack of a link (rābiṭ). The second: that it is on its normal footing, and its nominative is by resumption. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «It, that is the story, and «تُصْبِحُ» is the khabar.» I (al-Samīn) say: there is no need to imply a mubtadaʾ; rather this is a resumptive verbal sentence, especially as he implied the mubtadaʾ as the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa) and then omitted it, which is not permissible, because the pronoun of the story is brought only for emphasis and magnification, and omission contradicts that.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: why was it not said «فأصبحتْ», and why was it turned to the form of the imperfect? I say: for a point in it, namely to convey the persistence of the effect of the rain from time to time, as you say: «So-and-so favoured me in such-and-such a year, so I go out in the evening and the morning thankful to him.» Had you said «I went in the evening and I went in the morning», it would not have fallen into that place. If you ask: then why is it nominative and not accusative as the answer to the question? I say: had it been accusative it would give the opposite of the purpose, because its meaning is the affirmation of greenness, and with the accusative it turns into the negation of greenness. An example is that you say to your companion: «Have you not seen that I favoured you, so you give thanks?» If you put it in the accusative, you are negating his thanks and complaining of his negligence [in it]; and if you put it in the nominative, you are affirming the thanks. This and its like are matters for which one who is marked by knowledge should have a desire in the science of i'rab and respect for its people.» Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «His saying «فتصبحُ» is equivalent to His saying «فتضحى» or «تصير», an expression of its haste after the descent of the water and its continuing so by habit. The nominative of His saying «فتُصْبِحُ» is because the verse is a report (khabar), and the fāʾ is a conjunction and not an answer, because its being an answer to His saying {أَلَمْ تَرَ} is corrupt in meaning.»
The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: «Neither he nor al-Zamakhsharī before him explained how the accusative would negate greenness, except for the meaning being corrupt. Sībawayh said: «I asked him, meaning al-Khalīl, about {أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ الله أَنزَلَ مِنَ السمآء مَآءً فَتُصْبِحُ الأرض مُخْضَرَّةً}, and he said: this is an affirmative and an alert (wājib wa-tanbīh), as though you had said: «Do you hear that Allah sent down water from the sky, and so it was such and such?»» Ibn Kharūf said: his saying «this is wājib» and his saying «so it was such and such» means that both are past; and he explained the speech with «Do you hear» to show you that it is not connected to the question, because of the weakness of the force of the question in it. Some commentators on the Book (of Sībawayh) said: «the accusative of «فتصبحُ» is not possible, because the speech is affirmative. Do you not see that the meaning is: Allah sent down, so the earth is in this state?» Al-Farrāʾ said: ««أَلَمْ تَرَ» is a report, as you say in speech: «Know that Allah does such-and-such, and so such-and-such will be.»»
He says: «The accusative as an answer to the question is excluded here only because negation, when the question enters upon it, although it requires affirmation (taqrīr) in some speech, is treated like pure negation in the answer. Do you not see His saying, the Exalted: {أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُواْ بلى} [al-Aʿrāf: 172]? Likewise the answer with the fāʾ: when you answer a negation it is on two meanings, in each of which the answer is negated. If you say «mā ta'tīnā fa-tuḥaddithanā» with the accusative, the meaning is: «you do not come to us speaking; rather you come and do not speak.» And the meaning may be: «you do not come, so how would you speak?» So the speaking is negated in both cases. And affirmation (taqrīr) with the interrogative particle, like pure negation in the answer, affirms what the hamza enters upon and negates the answer. So from what we have established it follows that seeing is affirmed and greenness negated, which is contrary to the intended. Also, the answer to a question forms with the preceding question a condition and a consequence, as in his saying:
3396 - ألم تَسْألْ فَتُخْبِرْكَ الرُّسومُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Did you not ask, so that the ruins would tell you …)
which is implied as: «if you ask, the ruins will tell you.» Here it cannot be implied: «if you see the sending down of the rain, the earth becomes green», because its greenness is not consequent upon your knowledge or your seeing; it is consequent only upon the sending down. And he expressed it in the imperfect only because it gives a depiction of the state the earth is in and the condition that the earth is clothed in, whereas the past indicates the cutting off of a thing. This is like the saying of Jaḥdar ibn Maʿūna, describing his state in the most severe misfortune in a story that took place between him and al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf al-Thaqafī; they are verses, among them:
3397 - يَسْمُوا بناظِرَتَيْنِ تَحْسَبُ فيهما ... لِما أَجالهما شعاعَ سِراج
(He rises with two eyes in which you would think, from the way he rolled them, there were rays of a lamp)
لَمَّا نَزَلْتُ بحُصْنِ أَزْبَرَ مُهْصِرٍ ... للقِرْن أرواحَ العدا مَجَّاجِ
(When I came down to the fortress of a fierce, mauling lion, who spews out the lives of enemies against his rival)
فأكرٌّ أحملُ وهو يُقعي باسْته ... فإذا يعودُ فراجعٌ أدراجي
(So I charge and attack while he squats on his haunches; and when he returns, I go back the way I came)
وعلمْتُ أني إنْ أَبَيْتَ نِزالَه ... أني من الحَجَّاج لستُ بناجي
(And I knew that if I refused to fight him, I would not escape from al-Ḥajjāj)
So his saying «فأكرٌّ» is a depiction of the state he was in.»
I (al-Samīn) say: as for his saying «Also, the answer to a question forms with the preceding question…» up to his saying «…consequent only upon the sending down», it is taken from the speech of Abū l-Baqāʾ. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «The verb is nominative here although a question precedes it, for two reasons. One: that it is a question in the sense of a report, that is: «you have seen», so it has no answer. The second: that what follows the fāʾ is accusative when what is asked about is a cause of it, and his seeing the sending down of the water does not make the greenness of the earth necessary, it is only necessary from the water.» As for his saying «He expressed it in the imperfect only because…», it is exactly the meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's words; he only changed his wording and expanded it.
And His saying «فتصبحُ»: some used it as evidence that the fāʾ does not require immediate succession (taʿqīb), saying: «because its greenness is delayed after the sending down of the water, by observation.» This has been answered with what ʿIkrima transmitted: that the land of Mecca and Tihāma is as described, and that it is rained on at night and in the morning the land is green, so the fāʾ is on its normal footing. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «I witnessed this in the Far Sūs: rain fell at night after drought, and that sandy land which the winds blow over became green by morning with weak vegetation.» And it was said: the delay of each thing is according to its nature.
And it was said: there are omitted sentences before the fāʾ, its implied form being: «so it stirs, swells, and grows, and then it becomes…». This is shown by His saying {فَإِذَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا المآء اهتزت وَرَبَتْ وَأَنبَتَتْ}, and this is an omission indicated by the drift of the speech, like His saying, the Exalted: {فَأَرْسِلُونِ * يُوسُفُ أَيُّهَا الصديق أَفْتِنَا} [Yūsuf: 45-46] to the end of the story.
And «تُصْبِحُ» may be the incomplete (nāqiṣa) verb and may be the complete (tāmma). And «مُخْضَرَّةً» is a ḥāl; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it. There is a distance from the meaning in it, since the implication becomes: «so the earth enters the time of morning in this state.» It is also permissible that it be on its normal footing, indicating the coupling of the content of the sentence with this particular time. He singled out this time only because greenery and gardens are most delightful to see then. And it may mean «becomes» (taṣīr).
The majority read it with ḍamma on the mīm and shaddah on the rāʾ, an active participle of ikhḍarrat, so it is mukhḍarra. The original is mukhḍarira with kasra on the first rāʾ, which was assimilated into its like. Some read «مَخْضَرَة» with fatḥa on the mīm and light rāʾ, on the pattern of mabqala and masbaʿa. The meaning is: possessing greenery, possessing beasts of prey, possessing herbage.
[Translator's note: the source has misplaced quotation marks in this entry, and «وهو يُقعي باسْته» in the third verse is rendered literally; the glosses on the verses are mine.]

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His saying: {والفلك}: the majority read «الفلك» in the accusative, and there are two views on it. One: that it is conjoined to {مَّا فِي الأرض}, that is: "He subjected to you what is on the earth, and He subjected to you the ships". He mentioned it separately, although it falls by way of generality under «ما» in His saying {مَّا فِي الأرض}, because the favour is evident in it and its subjection is wondrous beyond the other subjected things. On this, «تَجْري» is a ḥāl. The second: that it is conjoined to the Majestic Name, with the implication: "Have you not seen that the ships run in the sea", so «تجري» is a khabar on this.
Al-Kisāʾī, in what he transmitted from al-Ḥasan, put a ḍamma on the lām of «الفُلُكَ» here, and it is the reading of Ibn Miqsam. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Ṭalḥa, al-Aʿraj, Abū Ḥaywa and al-Zaʿfarānī read «والفلكُ» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «تجري» after it as the khabar. It is also permissible that its nominative be conjoined to the position of the noun of «أنَّ», according to those who allow that, as in «inna Zaydan wa-ʿAmrun qāʾimān»; on this, «تجري» is also a ḥāl. And in «بأمرِه», the bāʾ is causal. His saying {أَن تَقَعَ}: there are three views on it. One: that it is in the position of accusative or genitive, because it is on the omission of the preposition, its implied form being «من أن تقعَ». The second: that it is in the position of accusative only, because it is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from «السماء», that is: "and He holds back its falling, He prevents it". The third: that it is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the Basrans imply "dislike of its falling", and the Kufans "lest it fall".
His saying: {إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ}: there are two views on this prepositional phrase. One: that it is attached to «تقعَ», that is: "except by His permission, and then it falls". The second: that it is attached to «يُمْسِكُ». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «It is possible that His saying {إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ} refers back to the holding back, because the speech requires "without pillars" and the like, as though He meant: "except by His permission, so by it He holds it".» The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: «Had it been as he said, the construction would have been «by His permission», without the particle of exception, and the implication would be: "and He holds the sky by His permission".» I (al-Samīn) say: this exception is "emptied" (mufarragh), and does not occur in an affirmative, but since the speech before it is in the force of a negation, that is permissible, the implication being: "He does not leave it to fall except by His permission". What appears is that this bāʾ is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), that is: "except connected with His command".

semin-durr:67-67.t:
His saying: {هُمْ نَاسِكُوهُ}: this sentence is an adjective (ṣifa) of «مَنْسَكاً». It has already been mentioned that it is read with fatḥa and with kasra, and the disagreement on it has been given: is it a maṣdar (verbal noun) or a place? Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «"nāsikūhu" implies that manṣak is the maṣdar; had it been a place he would have said "nāsikūna fīhi"», meaning that a verb is not made transitive to the pronoun of a locative except by means of «fī». What he said is not binding, because latitude may be taken with the locative so that it is treated as a direct object, and the verb reaches its pronoun directly, as with whatever functions as the verb does. An example of latitude with a locative of time is the saying:
3398 - ويومٍ شَهِدْنَاه سُلَيْمَى وعامراً ... قليلٍ سوى الطَّعْنِ النِّهالِ نوافِلُهْ
(Many a day we witnessed, Sulaymā and ʿĀmir, its spoils little but the thrusts of the thirsty spears)
and of latitude with a locative of place the saying:
3399 - ومَشْرَبٍ أَشْرَبُه وَشِيْلِ ... لا أَجِنِ الطَّعْمِ ولا وَبِيْلِ
(and a watering place I drink from, scant, neither stale in taste nor unwholesome)
he means: "I drink in it".
His saying: {فَلاَ يُنَازِعُنَّكَ}: it was also read with the light nūn. Abū Mijlaz read «فلا يَنْزِعُنَّك», from "such-and-such", that is: "I uprooted it from him". Al-Zajjāj said: «it is from nāzaʿtuhu fa-nazaʿtuhu anziʿuhu, that is: I overcame him in the dispute.» This verse comes like His saying, the Exalted: {فَلاَ يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا} and their saying: lā uraynnaka hāhunā. Here His saying {لِّكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ} came without a conjoining wāw, unlike its counterpart earlier, which has a wāw of conjunction. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Because «that one» occurred with verses near it and fitting with it in the matter of rites, so it was conjoined to its sisters; as for this one, it occurs among verses far from its meaning, so it found nothing to be conjoined to.»

semin-durr:72-72.t:
His saying: {تَعْرِفُ}: the majority read «تَعْرِف» in the address form, active; «المُنْكَرَ» is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi). ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «يُعْرَفُ» with the yāʾ, passive, and «المنكرُ» is nominative, standing in the place of the agent. And al-munkar is a noun of the maṣdar meaning inkār (denial). His saying {الذين كَفَرُواْ} is an instance of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, to add to what is said about them by that.
His saying: {يَكَادُونَ يَسْطُونَ}: this is a ḥāl, either from the relative noun, although it is a muḍāf ilayhi, because the muḍāf is part of it, or from «الوجوه» because it is used to refer to its owners, as in His saying {وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ} [ʿAbasa: 40], then He said «أولئك هم». And «يَسْطُون» includes the meaning of «يَبْطِشُون» (they assault), so it is made transitive as that is; otherwise it is transitive by «على», one says saṭā ʿalayhi. Its root is overpowering and prevailing. It was also said: displaying what terrifies in order to frighten. "So-and-so has saṭwa", that is, dominance and overpowering.
His saying: «النار» is read with the three vowels. The nominative is in two ways. One: the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar the sentence «وَعَدَها الله»; the sentence has no position, as it is explicative of the earlier «شر». It is as though it were said: "What is worse than that?" and it was said: "The Fire, Allah has promised it." The second: that it is a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, as though it were said: "What is worse than that?" and it was said: "The Fire", that is: "it is the Fire", and then «وعدها الله» may be nominative as a khabar after a khabar.
It was also allowed that it be a badal (substitute) from «النار». There is something to consider in this, in that the replaced noun is a single word. It may be answered that the sentence is in the interpretation of a single word, and it is a badal ishtimāl, as though it were said: "the Fire which Allah has promised the disbelievers". It was also allowed that it be resumptive with no position. It may not be a ḥāl. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «because in the sentence there is nothing fit to govern the ḥāl.» The apparent sense of the Shaykh's quotation from al-Zamakhsharī is that he allows it to be a ḥāl, for he said: «Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that «النار» be a mubtadaʾ and «وعدَها» a khabar, and that it be a ḥāl on the first i'rab.» End. The first i'rab is that «النار» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. But al-Zamakhsharī did not make it a ḥāl except if you put «النار» in the accusative or the genitive with an implied «قد»; this is his text. He prevented that only because of what was said earlier by Abū l-Baqāʾ, namely the absence of a governor.
The accusative, which is the reading of Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla, is in three ways. One: that it is accusative by an implied verb which the overt verb explains, the matter being one of ishtighāl (occupation). The second: that it is accusative as specification of praise or blame (ikhtiṣāṣ); al-Zamakhsharī said it. The third: that it is accusative by an implied «أعني» ("I mean"), which is close to the one before it or is the same.
The genitive, which is the reading of Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Ibrāhīm ibn Nūḥ, is as a badal from «شر».
As for the pronoun in «وعدها»: the Shaykh said: «The apparent is that it is the first object, on the basis that He, the Exalted, promised the Fire the disbelievers, that it would feed them to it. Do you not see His saying, the Exalted: {وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِن مَّزِيدٍ} [Qāf: 30]? It is also possible that the pronoun is the second object and {الذين كَفَرُواْ} the first object, as He said: {وَعَدَ الله الْمُنَافِقِينَ والمنافقات والكفار نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ} [al-Tawba: 68].» I (al-Samīn) say: this second ought to be definite, because whenever two things follow a verb that governs two objects, and the second is not a description of the first, the logical agent has priority in order and is the first object. By the logical agent we mean one from whom an action can arise. So if you say «waʿadtu Zaydan dīnāran», the dīnār is the (second) object because no action arises from it; and this is the like of «aʿṭaytu Zaydan dirhaman», where Zayd is the agent since he is the taker of the dirham.
His saying: {وَبِئْسَ المصير}: the specified (al-makhṣūṣ) is omitted. Its implied form is: "and wretched is the destination: it, the Fire".
[Translator's note: in the discussion of the pronoun the source's wording about "ought to be definite" (يتعين) and the final sentence is rendered literally; the Shaykh is Abū Ḥayyān.]

semin-durr:73-73.t:
His saying: {ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ}: al-Akhfash said: «There is no example here; rather the meaning is: the disbelievers made a likeness for Allah.» Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: what was brought is not an example, so why did He call it an example? I say: the description and the striking story received with approval and astonishment have been called an example, likening it to some of the circulating proverbs because it is astonishing and approved.» Another said: it is an example in meaning, because the example of one who worships idols was struck by one who worships what cannot create a fly.
The majority read «تَدْعُون» with the tāʾ of address. Al-Ḥasan, Yaʿqūb, Hārūn and Maḥbūb from Abū ʿAmr read it with the yāʾ, and in both it is active. Mūsā al-Aswārī and al-Yamānī read «يُدْعَوْن» with the yāʾ, passive.
His saying: {لَن يَخْلُقُواْ}: al-Zamakhsharī made the negation of «لن» one of perpetuity, and the discussion with him on that has already been given. The fly (dhubāb) is well known. It is pluralized as dhibbān and dhubbān, with kasra and ḍamma on the dhāl, and as dhubb. The midhabba is what flies are driven away with. It is a generic noun whose singular is dhubāba, used for the masculine and the feminine, so they are distinguished by description.
His saying: {وَلَوِ اجتمعوا لَهُ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: «accusative as a ḥāl, as though He said: their creating a fly is impossible, [even] on the condition that they all gather for creating it and help each other in it.» It has been said more than once that this wāw conjoins this circumstantial sentence to an omitted ḥāl, that is: "their creating a fly is negated in every state, even in this state which would call for their creating it, for the sake of the fly or for the sake of the idol."
As-salb is seizing a thing quickly. One says: salabahu niʿmatahu. And as-salab is what is on the slain man. In the ḥadīth: «Whoever kills a man, his salab is his.» Al-istinqādh is the istafʿala form with the meaning of the ifʿāl form; one says anqadhahu min kadhā, that is: he rescued him from it and freed him. Likewise aballa l-marīḍ and istaballa. As for His saying «ضَعُفَ الطالبُ» ("weak is the seeker"), it was said it is a report; it was said it is an expression of wonder, and the first is more apparent.

semin-durr:75-75.t: His saying: {الله يَصْطَفِي مِنَ الملائكة رُسُلاً وَمِنَ الناس}: it was said that its implied form is: "and from the people, messengers". There is no need for that; rather His saying {وَمِنَ الناس} is implied as fronted, that is: "He chooses from the angels, and from the people, messengers".

semin-durr:78-78.t:
His saying: {حَقَّ جِهَادِهِ}: it may be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and that is clear. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «It may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "striving, the true striving for Him".» There is something to consider in it, in that this is definite, so how can it be made an adjective of an indefinite? Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: what is the reason for this annexation, when the analogy would be "the true striving in Him" or "the true striving of yours in Him", as He said: {وَجَاهِدُوا فِي الله}? I say: annexation takes place by the slightest connection and specificity, so when striving is specific to Allah in that it is done for His sake and for His countenance, its annexation to Him is sound. Or latitude may be taken with the locative, as in the saying:
3400 - ويومٍ شَهِدْناه سليمى وعامِراً ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Many a day we witnessed, Sulaymā and ʿĀmir …)
By the locative he means the preposition and its genitive noun, as though the original were "the true striving in it", so the preposition was dropped and the maṣdar annexed to the pronoun; and it is of the type of «huwa ḥaqqu ʿālimin» and «jiddu ʿālimin», that is: truly a scholar and earnestly a scholar.»
His saying: {مِّلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ}: there are several views on it. One: that it is accusative by an implied «اتَّبِعوا» (follow); al-Ḥawfī said it, and Abū l-Baqāʾ followed him. The second: that it is by ikhtiṣāṣ, that is: "I mean, by the religion, the creed of your father". The third: that it is accusative by what precedes it, as though He had said: "He has widened your religion with a widening of the creed of your father", then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place; al-Zamakhsharī said it. The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied «جَعَلها» ("He made it"); Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it. The fifth: that it is accusative on the omission of the genitive kāf, that is: "like the creed of Ibrāhīm"; al-Farrāʾ said it, and Abū l-Baqāʾ said something close to it, for he said: «It was said that its implied form is "like the creed of", because the meaning is: "He made the religion easy for you like the creed of your father", so the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place.» The most apparent of these is the third. And «إبراهيم» is a badal or a bayān, or accusative by «أعني».
His saying: {هُوَ سَمَّاكُمُ}: there are two views on this pronoun. One: that it refers to «إبراهيم», for he is the nearest mentioned. However, Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «In this expression, meaning His saying «وفي هذا», is the weakness of the view of one who said the pronoun is for Ibrāhīm. It is not tenable except by implying an omission from the speech, as a resumption.» End. The meaning of "the weakness of the view of one who said that" is that His saying «وفي هذا» is conjoined to «مِنْ قبلُ», and «هذا» points to the Quran, which was sent down after Ibrāhīm by long periods; therefore his view is weak. As for his saying "except by implying an omission", what ought to be implied is: "and you have been named in this Quran the Muslims". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «It was said that the pronoun is for Ibrāhīm; on this view His saying «وفي هذا» means: "and in this Quran is the reason for their naming".» The second: that it refers to Allah, the Exalted, and the reading of Ubayy supports it: «الله سَمَّاكم» with the Majestic Name explicit, that is: "He named you in the earlier scriptures and in this noble Quran also".
His saying: {لِيَكُونَ الرسول} is attached to «سَمَّاكم».
And His saying: {فَنِعْمَ المولى}, that is: Allah. The omission of the specified (al-makhṣūṣ) is made good by the second occurring at the head of a verse and its end (fāṣila).

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {الذين أُخْرِجُواْ}: it may be in the position of genitive, as an adjective (naʿt) of the first relative noun, or an explication of it, or a badal (substitute) from it; and it may be in the position of accusative as praise (madḥ), and it may be in the position of nominative on an implied mubtadaʾ.
His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن يَقُولُواْ}: there are two views on it. One: that it is accusative as a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), and this is among what the Arabs agree to put in the accusative, because it is discontinuous and the governor cannot be directed to it, and whatever is so they agree to put in the accusative, as in «mā zāda illā mā naqaṣa» ("it did not increase except what it decreased") and «mā nafaʿa illā mā ḍarra» ("it did not benefit except what harmed"). Had the governor been able to be directed to it, two dialects would be permitted in it: the accusative, which is the dialect of the Hijaz, and that it be like the continuous in accusative and badal, as in «mā fīhā aḥadun illā ḥimārun». The noble verse is among those to which the governor cannot be directed, because if you said «alladhīna ukhrijū min diyārihim illā an yaqūlū rabbunā llāhu» it would not be sound. The second: that it is in the position of genitive as a badal from «حَقّ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: «that is, without any cause other than the affirmation of oneness (tawḥīd), which ought to be a cause for acknowledgement and establishment and not a cause for expulsion and driving away. Its like is: {هَلْ تَنقِمُونَ مِنَّآ إِلاَّ أَنْ آمَنَّا بالله} [al-Māʾida: 59].»
Among those who made it in the position of genitive as a badal from what precedes is al-Zajjāj. However, the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) rejected that, saying: «What the two allowed of badal is not permissible, because a badal is permissible only where a negation, prohibition or question with the sense of negation has preceded it. As for when the speech is affirmative or an imperative, the badal is not permissible, because a badal occurs only where the governor can be directed to it. If you said «qāma illā Zaydun» and «li-yaḍrib illā ʿAmrun» it would not be permitted. If you said, outside the Quran, «ukhrija l-nāsu min diyārihim illā bi-an yaqūlū lā ilāha illā llāhu», it would not be speech. This is when it is imagined that {إِلاَّ أَن يَقُولُواْ} is in the position of genitive as a badal from «غير» annexed to «حَقٍّ». But if it is a badal from «حق», as al-Zamakhsharī stated explicitly, it is extremely corrupt, because it follows that the badal comes right after «غير», so the construction becomes «bi-ghayri illā an yaqūlū», and this is not sound. And if we implied [illā] as «ghayr», as is implied in the negation in «mā marartu bi-aḥadin illā Zaydin», making it a badal, it would not be sound, because the construction becomes «bi-ghayri ghayri qawlihim rabbunā llāhu», so you would have annexed ghayr to ghayr, and they are the same, so it becomes "without other than"; whereas in «mā marartu bi-aḥadin illā Zaydin» it is sound to say «mā marartu bi-ghayri Zaydin». Then, al-Zamakhsharī, where he gave an example of the badal, implied it as "without a cause other than tawḥīd", and this is an example of the adjective (ṣifa), making [illā] mean "other than" (siwā), and that is sound on the ṣifa; so the chapter of the ṣifa was confused for him with the chapter of the badal. And it is permissible to say «marartu bi-l-qawmi illā Zaydin» on the ṣifa and not the badal.»
His saying: {وَلَوْلاَ دَفْعُ الله}: the disagreement on it has been given in al-Baqara, together with the explanation of the two readings.
Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr read «لَهُدِمَتْ» in the light form; the rest read it with the doubled form, which indicates multiplicity, because the places are many and various, and the first reading is also fit for this meaning.
The majority read «صَلَواتٌ» with fatḥa on the ṣād and the lām, plural of ṣalāh. Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad read «وصُلُوات» with ḍamma on both. It was also transmitted from him with kasra on the ṣād and sukūn on the lām. Al-Jaḥdarī read it with ḍamma on the ṣād and fatḥa on the lām. Abū l-ʿĀliya read it with fatḥa on the ṣād and sukūn on the lām. Al-Jaḥdarī also read «وصُلُوْت» with ḍamma on both and sukūn on the wāw, followed by a tāʾ with two dots above, like ṣulb and ṣulūb.
Al-Kalbī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk likewise, except that they put three dots on the tāʾ (thāʾ). Al-Jaḥdarī also, and Abū l-ʿĀliya, Abū Rajāʾ and Mujāhid likewise, except that they put an alif after the thāʾ and read «صُلُوْثا»; and it was transmitted from Mujāhid with the tāʾ with two dots above also. It was also transmitted from al-Jaḥdarī «صُلْواث» with ḍamma on the ṣād and sukūn on the lām and an alif after the wāw and a thāʾ.
ʿIkrima read «صلويثى» with kasra on the ṣād and sukūn on the lām, followed by a wāw with kasra, then a yāʾ with two dots below, then a thāʾ. Ibn Mujāhid reported that «صِلْواث» was read with kasra on the ṣād and sukūn on the lām, followed by a wāw, then an alif, then a thāʾ.
Al-Jaḥdarī read «وصُلُوب» like kuʿūb, with a bāʾ with one dot, which is the plural of «ṣalīb» (cross); and fuʿūl as a plural of faʿīl is anomalous, as in ẓarīf and ẓurūf, and asīna and usūn. It was transmitted from Abū ʿAmr «صلواتُ» like the majority, except that he gave no tanwīn, prohibiting full declension for being a proper name and foreign, because he made it the name of a place. These are fourteen readings, of which one is famous, namely this well-known prayer (ṣalāh).
An omitted muḍāf must be implied for the demolition to be directed to them soundly, that is: "places of prayers"; or «هُدِّمَتْ» includes the meaning of «عُطِّلَتْ» (were put out of use), so it is a common measure between places and acts, for the disabling of everything is according to its kind. He put the mosques last for their later coming into being, or to move to the most noble. And the ṣalawāt among the nations . . . the prayer of each creed according to it. The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words is that it is by itself a noun of place, for he said: «The church was called ṣalāt because it is prayed in. It was also said: it is an Arabized word whose origin in Hebrew is ṣalūthā.» End.
As for other readings than it, it was said: they are Syriac or Hebrew entering the tongue of the Arabs; for that reason the dialects in it are many.
Ṣawāmiʿ is the plural of ṣawmaʿa, which is a tall, sharp-topped building, from their saying "aṣmaʿ man", who is sharp of speech. Its pattern is fawʿala, like dawkhala. It is the place of worship of monks because they live apart. It was also said: the place of worship of the Sabians.
Biyaʿ is the plural of biyʿa, the place of worship of the Christians. It was also said: the synagogues of the Jews.
The best-known is that the ṣawāmiʿ are for monks, the biyaʿ for Christians, the ṣalawāt for Jews, and the mosques for Muslims.
And {يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا اسم الله} may be an adjective of all the places mentioned earlier, if we return the pronoun in «فيها» to them, or an adjective of the mosques only, if we restrict the pronoun in «فيها» to them; the first is more apparent.
[Translator's note: the passage «والصلواتُ في الأمم. . . . . . صلاةُ كلِّ مِلَّةٍ بحَسَبِها» contains a gap marked by dots in the source.]

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {فَكَأَيِّن مِّن قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا}: «كأيِّنْ» may be accusative in position by ishtighāl (occupation) with an implied verb which «أهلكناها» explains, and may be in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «أَهْلكناها» the khabar. The verification of the matter has already been given.
His saying: {وَهِيَ ظَالِمَةٌ}: a circumstantial sentence from the hāʾ of «أَهْلكناها».
His saying: {فَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ}: conjoined to «أَهْلَكْناها», so it may be in the position of nominative by being conjoined to the khabar on the second view, and may have no position by being conjoined to the explicative sentence on the first view. This is what al-Zamakhsharī meant by his saying: «The second, meaning His saying {فَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ}, has no position because it is conjoined to «أهلكناها», and this verb has no position», as a consequence of the view of ishtighāl. Otherwise, if we say that it is the khabar of «كأيِّن», it would necessarily have a position.
Abū ʿAmr read «أهلكتُها»; the rest read «أَهْلكناها», and both are clear.
His saying: {وَبِئْرٍ مُّعَطَّلَةٍ}: conjoined to «قريةٍ», and likewise «قَصْرٍ», that is: "and how many a well and a palace We destroyed also". This is the view. There is a second view in it: that it is conjoined, with what follows it, to «عروشِها», that is: "fallen upon well and palace also". That is nothing.
Bir (well) is from baʾartu l-arḍa, that is, "I dug it". From it comes al-taʾbīr, which is splitting [the date-spathe] (al-ṭalʿ). Al-bir is a fiʿl with the meaning of maf ʿūl, like al-dhibḥ meaning "the slaughtered", and it is feminine, though it may be masculine in the sense of qalīb (well). And the saying:
3395 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وبِئْري ذو حَفَرْتُ وذو طَوَيْتُ
(… and my well is that which I dug and that which I lined)
admits the masculine and the feminine. Al-muʿaṭṭala is the neglected, and taʿṭīl is neglect. It was also read «مُعْطَلَةٍ» in the light form; one says aʿṭaltu l-bira and ʿaṭṭaltuhā, so it became idle (ʿaṭalat) with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ, whereas "the woman was bare of ornaments" is ʿaṭilat with kasra on the ṭāʾ. As for al-mashīd, it has already been said that it means "raised high" or "plastered". It is built here from shādahu, and in al-Nisāʾ from shayyadahu, because there it is after a plural so the intensive suits, and here it is after a singular so the light form suits, and because it is at the head of a verse and its ending.
[Translator's note: the source has a gap marked by dots after "splitting" («وهو شَقُّ. . . . . . الطلع»); the translation reads "the date-spathe" for الطلع only, and the gap is not filled.]

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {فَتَكُونَ}: it is accusative as the answer to the question. Al-Ḥawfī's wording is "as the answer to affirmation". It was also said: as the answer to negation. Mubashshir ibn ʿUbayd read «فيكونَ» with the yāʾ, because the feminine is figurative. What the verb is attached to is omitted, that is: "what befell the earlier nations".
His saying: {فَإِنَّهَا لاَ تَعْمَى}: the pronoun is the pronoun of the story (ḍamīr al-qiṣṣa), and {لاَ تَعْمَى الأبصار} explains it. The feminine in the pronoun is made good by the fact that a verb with a feminine mark follows it, and had it been masculine in speech, so that "fa-innahu" was said, it would have been permissible; and this is a reading transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh, the masculine being with regard to the matter and the affair. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It may be a vague pronoun explained by «الأبصارُ», and in «تَعْمَى» it is a pronoun returning to it.» The Shaykh said: «What he mentioned is not permissible, because that which is explained by what follows it is limited, and this is not one of them: it is in the chapter of «rubba», in the chapter of niʿma and biʾsa, in the chapter of iʿmāl, in the chapter of badal, in the chapter of mubtadaʾ and khabar (with disagreement over some of them), and in the chapter of the pronoun of the affair (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the first five are explained by a single word except the pronoun of the affair, which is explained by a sentence, and this is not one of the six.»
I (al-Samīn) say: rather this is one of the places mentioned, and it is the chapter of the mubtadaʾ. The most that can be said is that an abrogating particle entered upon it, namely «inna», so it is the like of their saying: «hiya l-ʿarab taqūlu mā shāʾat», «hiya l-nafs tataḥammalu mā ḥammalat», and His saying, the Exalted: {إِنْ هِيَ إِلاَّ حَيَاتُنَا} [al-Anʿām: 29]. Al-Zamakhsharī made all of that among what is explained by what follows it, and there is no difference between the noble verse and these examples except the entry of the abrogating particle, which has no effect; and I was surprised at the Shaykh's inattention to that.
His saying: {التي فِي الصدور}: an adjective, or a badal, or an explication. Is it an emphasis, because hearts are not anywhere but in the chests, or does it have an additional meaning? As al-Zamakhsharī said: «What has become customary and is held is that blindness in reality has its place in the eyesight, which is that the pupil is struck with something that effaces its light, and its use for the heart is a metaphor and a simile. When it was wished to establish what is contrary to the held belief, namely the ascription of blindness to the hearts in reality and its negation from the eyes, this depiction needed an added specification and an excess of definition, so that it be established that the place of blindness is the hearts and not the eyes, as you say: "The sharpness is not for the sword, but for your tongue that is between your jaws." Your saying "that is between your jaws" is an affirmation of what you claimed for his tongue and a confirmation, because the place of sharpness is that and nothing else, as though you said: "I did not negate sharpness from the sword and affirm it for your tongue by a slip of mine or an oversight, but I deliberately meant it by it, that very thing, deliberately.""
The Shaykh rejected the saying of Abū l-Qāsim, «taʿammadtu bihi iyyāhu» ("I deliberately meant it by it"), and made this wording a foreignism (ʿujma) in that he separated the pronoun, which is not a place for separating it, and the right would have been to say «taʿammadtuhu bihi», as you say «al-sayfu ḍarabtuka bihi» and not «ḍarabtu bihi iyyāka».
I say: you have already seen the like of this objection, and its answer, by what was answered concerning His saying, the Exalted: {يُخْرِجُونَ الرسول وَإِيَّاكُمْ} [al-Mumtaḥana: 1] and {وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الذين أُوتُواْ الكتاب مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 131]: namely that, with the intention of putting something other than the pronoun before it for a purpose, its attachment is barred; and what mistake is there in the like of this that foreignism should be claimed against one eloquent, to whom even his enemies attest that, though he may err in some beliefs that have no connection with what we are dealing with?
The Imam Fakhr al-Dīn (al-Rāzī) said: «There is another view on it in my opinion: the heart may be made a metonym for thought and reflection, as in His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لذكرى لِمَن كَانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ} [Qāf: 37]. According to a group, the seat of remembrance is the brain, so Allah, the Exalted, made clear that its seat is the chest.» And the seat of the intellect is a well-known disagreement. Ibn ʿAṭiyya inclined to the first; he said: «It is exaggeration, as you say: "I looked at him with my eye", and as in "they say with their mouths".» I say: I have shown a benefit in His saying «بأفواههم» beyond emphasis.
